definition_zh: 亲爱的；昂贵的；亲爱的（称呼）
definition_en: much loved, used to address someone close; also high in price
core_image: 信纸开头那一声放轻了的称呼
scene: 她拆开信封，第一行就写着那声熟悉的称呼。Dear Tom, I hope you are well.
sceneCN: 这里 dear 指「亲爱的」（第 1 个义项：深爱的人或亲昵称呼）；句意是信一开头就用这声称呼问好。

collocations.zh: 尊敬的先生或女士（书信开头）

senses.title: Loved and close to the heart
senses.definition: much loved, used when speaking to someone close
senses.definitionCN: 非常喜爱，用来称呼亲近的人
senses.example: She wrote Dear Mum at the top of the page.
senses.exampleCN: 她在纸页最上面写下「亲爱的妈妈」。
senses.why: A letter opens with the name of the person held closest.
senses.whyCN: 一封信总是从最亲近的那个人的称呼开始。

senses.title: Costing a lot of money
senses.definition: high in price, often higher than one expects
senses.definitionCN: 价钱高，常常高过人们的预期
senses.example: Fresh fruit is dear in the winter months.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天里新鲜水果很贵。
senses.why: What is precious has always been something you must pay for.
senses.whyCN: 珍贵的东西，从来都要付出代价才能得到。

senses.title: A small cry of feeling
senses.definition: a short exclamation of surprise, pity or worry
senses.definitionCN: 表示惊讶、惋惜或担心的短促感叹
senses.example: Oh dear, the last train has gone.
senses.exampleCN: 哎呀，末班车已经开走了。
senses.why: A sudden feeling wants a short sound rather than a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 突然涌上的情绪，只需要一个短音，用不着整句话。

intro.en: Dear is an old English word for precious, from a Germanic root that meant to hold in honour.
intro.cn: dear 是英语里表示珍贵的古老词，来自一个意为敬重的日耳曼词根。

items.en: The root carried the sense of something valued highly.
items.cn: 这个词根带着「被看得很重」的意思。

items.en: Deore meant precious or costly before it meant loved.
items.cn: deore 先指珍贵、价高，后来才指被爱。

items.en: Letter writers began opening with dear as a mark of respect.
items.cn: 写信的人开始在开头用 dear 表示敬意。

items.en: The exclamation oh dear appeared for small troubles.
items.cn: 表示小麻烦的感叹语 oh dear 出现了。

items.en: Dear stays warm in letters and formal in complaints about price.
items.cn: 如今 dear 在信里显得亲热，在抱怨价钱时又显得正式。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by a single vowel sound, and the meaning group runs from loved to expensive.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音，近义组则从心爱一路走到昂贵。

entries.definition: a wild animal that eats grass and has long legs
to be brave enough to do something
the head of a faculty in a university
entries.definitionCN: 大学里某个学院的院长

entries.definition: greatly loved by many people
of great value and not to be lost
costing a lot of money or effort
entries.definitionCN: 花费大量金钱或代价的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a name at the top of a letter and end with a price that is too high.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从信纸上的一句称呼开始，落到一个太高的价钱。

normal.en: A letter always begins with the person you would run to first.
normal.cn: 一封信总是从你最先想跑去找的那个人写起。

normal.en: The dearest thing in the shop is also the dearest thing in your heart.
normal.cn: 店里最贵的东西，往往也是心里最珍贵的东西。

normal.en: Dear is a word you say softly, never shout.
normal.cn: dear 是要轻声说出的词，从来不用喊。

normal.en: When the price hurts, the shopkeeper calls it dear.
normal.cn: 价钱让人心疼时，店家就说它贵。

normal.en: Two letters dropped from the middle turn deer into dear.
normal.cn: 中间少一个字母，鹿就变成了亲爱的。

abstract.en: Picture a hand writing a name slowly at the top of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在纸页最上方慢慢写下一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag that makes you put the fruit back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个价签让你把水果又放了回去。

abstract.en: Picture a small sigh let out when the bus pulls away.
abstract.cn: 想象公交车开走时，嘴边漏出的那声轻叹。

examples.en: Dear Anna, thank you for your long letter.
examples.cn: 亲爱的安娜，谢谢你写来这么长的信。

examples.en: Houses near the station are dearer than those outside town.
examples.cn: 车站附近的房子比城外的贵。

examples.en: Oh dear, I have left my keys inside.
examples.cn: 哎呀，我把钥匙落在里面了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dear 记成「惦记」：d 是门，ear 是耳朵，站在门口听见熟悉的声音，就是心里最惦记的人。

root: 源自古英语 deore（珍贵的、价高的），更早来自日耳曼语词根，本义是「被看得很重」。中古英语时期，写信的人开始用它作敬称；十八世纪又出现只表示惊讶或惋惜的感叹用法，珍贵、亲爱、昂贵三种意思其实都从「看重」长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From a name written with love, to a price that is too high, to a sigh over a small loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 从带着爱意写下的称呼，到高得让人犹豫的价钱，再到为小损失发出的叹息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name written softly at the top of a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸页最上方被轻轻写下的一个名字。

branches.en: The first sense is the person the heart keeps nearest.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是心里放得最近的那个人。

branches.en: The same value, counted in coins, becomes a high price.
branches.cn: 同样的看重，用钱来数，就成了高价。

branches.en: A feeling too quick for a sentence comes out as one short sound.
branches.cn: 来不及说成句子的情绪，就化成一声短叹。

branches.en: Both senses measure worth, one in the heart and one in the purse.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在衡量价值，一个用心，一个用钱包。

branches.en: Warmth and worry are the two voices of the same affection.
branches.cn: 亲热与担忧，是同一份牵挂发出的两种声音。

intro.en: Dear forms a small family: adverbs of warmth and price, and a verb about making oneself liked.
intro.cn: dear 这一族不大：表示亲热与价高的副词，还有一个表示讨人喜欢的动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root in dear; the word comes from Old English deore.
latinIntro.cn: dear 没有拉丁词根，它直接来自古英语 deore。

items.example: She is a dear friend of mine.
items.exampleCN: 她是我的一位好朋友。

items.meaning: very much, or at a high cost
items.example: He loved his little boat dearly.
items.exampleCN: 他非常喜爱自己的小船。

items.meaning: the state of being loved or costly
items.example: The dearness of fruit surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 水果之贵让我们吃了一惊。

items.example: He wrote to his dearest every week.
items.exampleCN: 他每周给最亲爱的人写信。

items.example: Her honesty endeared her to the team.
items.exampleCN: 她的坦诚让全队都喜欢她。

items.example: He called her by a childhood endearment.
items.exampleCN: 他用小时候的昵称叫她。

items.example: It was a dear-bought lesson.
items.exampleCN: 这是代价高昂的一课。

items.example: He got a dear John letter that spring.
items.exampleCN: 那年春天他收到一封分手信。

definition_en: the end of life; the permanent stopping of the body
core_image: 一盏灯被吹熄，屋里只剩沉默
scene: 老人在睡梦中安静地走了，屋里的人久久没有出声。His death came quietly in the night.
sceneCN: 这里 death 指「死亡」（第 1 个义项：生命的终止）；句意是他夜里安静地离世。

senses.title: The end of a life
senses.definition: the moment when a living body stops working for ever
senses.definitionCN: 活着的身体永远停止运转的那一刻
senses.example: His death came quietly in the night.
senses.exampleCN: 他在夜里安静地离世。
senses.why: A life that stops leaves a shape everyone around can feel.
senses.whyCN: 生命一停，周围每个人都能感到空出来的那一块。

senses.title: The end of something
senses.definition: the permanent end of a thing, idea or practice
senses.definitionCN: 事物、观念或做法永久结束
senses.example: The new road meant the death of many small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新修的路意味着许多小店的终结。
senses.why: We lend the word to anything that stops for good.
senses.whyCN: 凡是彻底停止的东西，我们都借这个词来说。

senses.title: Death as a figure
senses.definition: death imagined as a person or a force
senses.definitionCN: 被想象成一个人或一股力量的形象
senses.example: In the old painting, Death waits at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 在那幅古画里，死神等在门口。
senses.why: Giving death a body makes an unseen force easier to face.
senses.whyCN: 给死亡一个身体，看不见的力量就好面对一些。

intro.en: Death is an Old English noun from a Germanic root that also gave die and dead.
intro.cn: death 是古英语名词，来自一个同时长出 die 和 dead 的日耳曼词根。

items.en: Dauthuz named the act of dying among the old Germanic peoples.
items.cn: dauthuz 在古日耳曼语里指「死去」这件事。

items.en: Deaþ covered both the event and the state of being dead.
items.cn: deaþ 既指死亡这件事，也指死后的状态。

items.en: The noun kept its sound while the verb changed to die.
items.cn: 名词保住读音，动词却变成了 die。

items.en: Personified Death appeared in plays, carrying a scythe.
items.cn: 拟人化的死神拿着镰刀出现在戏剧里。

items.en: Death now also names the end of a language, a habit or a hope.
items.cn: 如今 death 也用来指语言、习惯或希望的终结。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same opening letters, and the meaning group moves from dying to a formal word for it.
note.cn: 形近组开头字母相同，近义组则从「垂死」一路走到正式的「逝世」。

entries.definition: unable to hear
money that you owe to someone
the distance from top to bottom
the process of losing life
a formal word for death or ending
entries.definitionCN: 死亡或结束的正式说法

entries.definition: the point where something stops

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a lamp going out and end with a word borrowed for things that stop.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一盏熄灭的灯开始，落到被借来说「停止」的用法。

normal.en: A room is not empty after the lamp goes out; it is quieter.
normal.cn: 灯灭之后屋子并不空，只是更安静。

normal.en: Breath is a sound you hear only when it stops.
normal.cn: 呼吸只有在停下时，才被人听见。

normal.en: Old plays put a scythe in the hand of death so the eye could see it.
normal.cn: 古戏给死神一把镰刀，是为了让眼睛看得见它。

normal.en: Shops and languages die the same way: nobody comes any more.
normal.cn: 店铺和语言是同样的死法：再没有人来。

normal.en: One letter apart, deaf and death both take away a sound.
normal.cn: deaf 和 death 只差一个字母，都带走了声音。

abstract.en: Picture a chair still warm after the person has left it.
abstract.cn: 想象人离开后，椅子还是温的。

abstract.en: Picture a candle with no flame and a thin line of smoke.
abstract.cn: 想象一支没有火苗、只剩细烟的蜡烛。

abstract.en: Picture a shop sign taken down and the hooks left bare.
abstract.cn: 想象店招被摘下，墙上只剩空钩子。

examples.en: His death came quietly in the night.
examples.cn: 他在夜里安静地离世。

examples.en: The death rate in the region has fallen in ten years.
examples.cn: 这个地区的死亡率十年间下降了。

examples.en: The new road meant the death of many small shops.
examples.cn: 新修的路意味着许多小店的终结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 death 记成「灯熄」：d 是灯，eath 念起来像呼吸，呼吸一停，灯就熄了。

root: 源自古英语 deaþ，更早是日耳曼语 dauthuz，与 die、dead 同出一根。它先指「死去」这件事与死后的状态，十四世纪起在道德剧里被拟人化为拿镰刀的形象，后来又被借去指语言、行业与希望的终结。

sensesIntro.en: From a body stopping, to anything ending for good, to a figure standing at the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体停止运转，到任何事物永久结束，再到站在门口的那个形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp blown out in a room that has gone silent.
core.cn: 核心意象：屋子里灯被吹熄，四下安静下来。

branches.en: The first sense is simply the body stopping for ever.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是身体永远停了下来。

branches.en: The same stopping, seen in a shop or a language, becomes an ending.
branches.cn: 同样的停止放到店铺或语言身上，就成了终结。

branches.en: An unseen force is given a face so that people can speak of it.
branches.cn: 看不见的力量被安上一张脸，人们才好谈论它。

branches.en: The event and the figure are the same idea, one felt and one drawn.
branches.cn: 事件与形象是同一个念头，一个被感受，一个被画出来。

branches.en: Both senses soften a hard fact by naming it another way.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在换一种说法，让硬邦邦的事实软一些。

intro.en: Death gathers a set of compounds about the end of life, from the bed to the sentence.
intro.cn: death 聚起一批与临终有关的复合词，从床铺一直到判决。

latinIntro.en: Death has no Latin element; Latin expressed the same idea with mors and mortis.
latinIntro.cn: death 里没有拉丁成分，拉丁语用 mors、mortis 表达同一个意思。

items.example: They spoke of his death with great care.
items.exampleCN: 他们提起他的死时非常小心。

items.example: A deathly silence filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 大厅里一片死寂。

items.example: The poem won deathless fame.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗赢得了不朽的名声。

items.meaning: the bed of a dying person
items.example: He made a promise at his father's deathbed.
items.exampleCN: 他在父亲临终的床前许下承诺。

items.example: The ruling was a deathblow to the plan.
items.exampleCN: 这项裁决对那个计划是致命打击。

items.meaning: the number of deaths in a group
items.example: The death rate fell after the new clinic opened.
items.exampleCN: 新诊所开张后死亡率下降了。

items.example: The death toll rose during the night.
items.exampleCN: 夜里死亡人数上升了。

items.meaning: a legal order to kill someone
items.example: The court gave him a death sentence.
items.exampleCN: 法庭判他死刑。

definition_en: a formal discussion in which two sides argue for opposing views
core_image: 两排人隔着长桌来回交锋
scene: 议会里两派人为预算争了一整个下午。The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 debate 指「辩论」（第 1 个义项：正式的对立讨论）；句意是两派明天再辩预算。

senses.title: Formal argument between two sides
senses.definition: an organised discussion in which two sides defend opposite views
senses.definitionCN: 两种立场各持一方、有秩序地进行的讨论
senses.example: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。
senses.why: Two claims meet in public and each must answer the other.
senses.whyCN: 两种主张当众相遇，谁都得回答对方。

senses.title: A long argument among people
senses.definition: a serious argument among people who disagree
senses.definitionCN: 意见不同的人之间较真的争吵
senses.example: The plan caused a heated debate at the dinner table.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划在饭桌上引起了一场激烈的争论。
senses.why: Even without a chair or a rule book, people still take sides.
senses.whyCN: 就算没有主席和规则，人们照样会分成两边。

senses.title: To weigh a choice in the mind
senses.definition: to turn a choice over and over before deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在下决心之前反复掂量一个选择
senses.example: She debated whether to call him that night.
senses.exampleCN: 她那晚反复斟酌要不要打电话给他。
senses.why: A private argument is still a debate, held inside one head.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的内心争辩，也是一场辩论，只是发生在脑袋里。

intro.en: Debate came from Old French debatre, to fight or contend, built on Latin battuere, to beat.
intro.cn: debate 来自古法语 debatre（争斗），根源是拉丁语 battuere（击打）。

items.en: Battuere meant to beat or strike with a weapon.
items.cn: battuere 指用武器击打。

items.en: Debatre meant to struggle, with words as often as with arms.
items.cn: debatre 指争斗，用嘴和用兵器一样常见。

items.en: Debate entered English as both a quarrel and a formal argument.
items.cn: debate 进入英语时，既指争吵也指正式辩论。

items.en: Parliament gave the word its ordered, public sense.
items.cn: 议会赋予这个词有秩序、公开进行的含义。

items.en: Debate also means to weigh a private choice.
items.cn: 如今 debate 也指在心里掂量一个选择。

note.en: The look-alike group all carry a sharp middle sound, and the meaning group runs from calm talk to open dispute.
note.cn: 形近组中间都有一个清亮的音，近义组则从平和的商谈走到公开的争端。

entries.definition: money taken out of an account
money paid back after a purchase
money that you owe
to talk about something with others
to speak angrily because you disagree
entries.definitionCN: 因为意见不同而带火气地说话

entries.definition: a serious disagreement that lasts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with two rows of speakers and end with one person arguing inside his own head.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从两排发言的人开始，落到一个人在自己脑子里争辩。

normal.en: A debate needs two sides, or it is only a speech.
normal.cn: 辩论得有两边，否则只是一场演讲。

normal.en: The stronger claim is the one that can answer back.
normal.cn: 更强的那个主张，是能回应对手的那个。

normal.en: Rules do not end the anger; they only keep it in chairs.
normal.cn: 规则不能消掉火气，只把火气按在椅子上。

normal.en: At dinner the debate begins over the salt and ends over politics.
normal.cn: 饭桌上的争论从盐罐开始，到政治结束。

normal.en: A mind that debates itself has two good speakers.
normal.cn: 在心里自我辩论的人，有两个好辩手。

abstract.en: Picture two hands raised at the same moment in a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象大厅里两只手在同一刻举起。

abstract.en: Picture a table where the same sentence is said twice, louder.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子上，同一句话被说了两遍，一遍比一遍响。

abstract.en: Picture a man walking home arguing with someone who is not there.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走回家，一路和不在场的人争辩。

examples.en: The two sides will debate the budget again tomorrow.
examples.cn: 两派明天将再次就预算展开辩论。

examples.en: Her decision caused a heated debate among the staff.
examples.cn: 她的决定在员工中引起了激烈争论。

examples.en: He debated for a long time before answering.
examples.cn: 他斟酌了很久才回答。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debate 记成「对掰」：de 是相对，bate 像 bat（球拍），两边各拿一块拍子来回对打，就是辩论。

root: 经古法语 debatre（争斗）进入英语，更早来自拉丁语 battuere（击打），所以辩论本来带着「交手」的意味。十四世纪入英语时兼指争吵与正式论辩，十六世纪议会用它指有秩序的公开讨论，现代又添了在心里反复权衡的意思。

sensesIntro.en: From two sides striking with words, to an argument at dinner, to a choice weighed alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从两边用言语交手，到饭桌上的争吵，再到独自掂量一个选择。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rows of people trading blows with words across a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两排人隔着桌子，用言语来回交手。

branches.en: The first sense is the ordered contest, watched by a room.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是有秩序的较量，满屋的人看着。

branches.en: Take away the rules and the same contest becomes a quarrel.
branches.cn: 拿掉规则，同一场较量就成了争吵。

branches.en: The contest turns inward when one person holds both sides.
branches.cn: 当一个人同时站在两边，较量就转向了内心。

branches.en: Both are people disagreeing; only the setting has changed.
branches.cn: 两者都是人在意见相左，只是场合不同。

branches.en: A loud argument and a silent one share the same shape.
branches.cn: 大声的争吵和无声的争辩，形状是一样的。

intro.en: Debate has a short family: the person, the quality of being open to question, and a few fixed compounds.
intro.cn: debate 这一族很短：辩论的人、可争议的性质，还有几个固定搭配。

latinIntro.en: The Latin element is battuere, to beat; the modern word keeps the idea of verbal blows.
latinIntro.cn: 其中的拉丁成分是 battuere（击打），现代词仍保留言语交手的意味。

items.meaning: to argue formally or weigh a choice
items.example: They debate every Friday in the club.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周五在社团里辩论。

items.meaning: a person who argues in a debate
items.example: She is the best debater in her class.
items.exampleCN: 她是班上最会辩论的人。

items.example: Whether the plan will work is debatable.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划是否行得通还有争议。

items.example: He joined the debating society.
items.exampleCN: 他加入了辩论社。

items.example: The motion passed undebated.
items.exampleCN: 这项动议未经辩论就通过了。

items.meaning: a group that competes in argument
items.example: Our debate team won the regional final.
items.exampleCN: 我们的辩论队赢了地区决赛。

items.meaning: a club where members practise arguing
items.example: The debate club meets on Wednesdays.
items.exampleCN: 辩论社每周三活动。

items.example: The council held an open debate on the plan.
items.exampleCN: 委员会就这个计划举行了公开辩论。

definition_en: money that you owe to a person or a bank
core_image: 账本上一行还没有划掉的红字
scene: 他把最后一笔欠款还清，账本终于合上了。It took him six years to pay off the debt.
sceneCN: 这里 debt 指「债务」（第 1 个义项：欠别人的钱）；句意是他用六年时间还清了债。

senses.title: Money that must be paid back
senses.definition: money borrowed and still owed to a person or a bank
senses.definitionCN: 借来尚未还给个人或银行的钱
senses.example: It took him six years to pay off the debt.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了六年才还清这笔债。
senses.why: Borrowing opens a line that stays open until it is closed.
senses.whyCN: 借钱是在账上开一道口子，还清之前它一直敞着。

senses.title: An obligation of thanks
senses.definition: a feeling of duty towards someone who has helped you
senses.definitionCN: 对帮助过自己的人怀有的亏欠之感
senses.example: She owes a debt to the teacher who believed in her.
senses.exampleCN: 她欠那位相信她的老师一份情。
senses.why: Help given freely still leaves a weight to be carried.
senses.whyCN: 别人白给的帮助，也会在心里留下一份要背的重量。

intro.en: Debt goes back to Latin debitum, a thing owed, from debere, to owe; the silent b is a scholar's gift.
intro.cn: debt 上溯到拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），源于 debere（欠），不发音的 b 是学者的手笔。

items.en: Debitum meant a thing owed, built on debere, to owe.
items.cn: debitum 指所欠之物，来自 debere（欠）。

items.en: Old French dette dropped the b in both sound and spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 dette 在读和写上都去掉了 b。

items.en: English took dette from French and used it for money and favours.
items.cn: 英语从法语借来 dette，既指钱也指人情。

items.en: Scholars restored the b to show the Latin source; the sound stayed as it was.
items.cn: 学者把 b 加回去以显示拉丁来源，读音却没有变。

items.en: The silent b survives as a small monument to Latin.
items.cn: 这个不发音的 b 留了下来，成了拉丁语的一座小纪念碑。

note.en: The look-alike group hides letters that are not spoken, and the meaning group names what is owed.
note.cn: 形近组里都藏着不发音的字母，近义组则都在说「欠着的东西」。

entries.definition: an amount taken out of an account
entries.definitionCN: 从账户中划出的一笔钱

entries.definition: a feeling of not being sure
a short written form of department
money lent that must be returned
a duty that you must carry out
a debt recorded in accounts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a line in a ledger and end with a favour that no money can clear.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从账本上的一行字开始，落到用钱还不清的那份情。

normal.en: A debt is a door left open until the last payment shuts it.
normal.cn: 债是一扇门，最后一笔还款才把它关上。

normal.en: Interest is time turned into money.
normal.cn: 利息就是把时间换成了钱。

normal.en: The b in debt is heard by no one and seen by everyone.
normal.cn: debt 里的 b 谁也听不见，却谁都看得见。

normal.en: Borrowing feels light in the hand and heavy at night.
normal.cn: 借钱时手上很轻，夜里却沉。

normal.en: Some debts are paid in visits, not in coins.
normal.cn: 有些债要靠探望来还，而不是靠钱。

abstract.en: Picture a red line in a ledger that no one has crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上一行没人划掉的红字。

abstract.en: Picture an empty purse and a calendar full of dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一只空钱包和一本写满日期的日历。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that helped you once, still held out.
abstract.cn: 想象一只曾帮过你的手，还伸在那里。

examples.en: It took him six years to pay off the debt.
examples.cn: 他花了六年才还清这笔债。

examples.en: The company is deep in debt after two bad years.
examples.cn: 公司经历两个坏年头后债台高筑。

examples.en: She owes a debt to the doctor who saved her son.
examples.cn: 她欠那位救了她儿子的医生一份情。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 debt 记成「待」：b 不发音像躲起来，剩下 det 念起来像「待」，欠了钱就得一直待着等还。

root: 源自拉丁语 debitum（所欠之物），动词 debere 意为「欠」。古法语作 dette，把 b 从读音和拼写里都去掉了；英语十三世纪借入，十六世纪学者又按拉丁原形把 b 补回拼写，读音仍旧不发，于是留下这个看得见听不见的字母。

sensesIntro.en: From a sum of money owed, to the weight of a kindness that cannot be counted.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一笔要还的钱，到一份数不清的人情。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an uncrossed line of red ink in a ledger.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一行没有被划掉的红字。

branches.en: The first sense is the sum borrowed and not yet returned.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是借来还没还的那笔钱。

branches.en: Kindness borrows the same shape, though no ledger records it.
branches.cn: 好意也长成同样的形状，只是没有账本记着。

branches.en: Money and gratitude both leave a person owing something.
branches.cn: 钱和恩情，都让人心里欠着点什么。

branches.en: Both senses explain why the word can be paid and also felt.
branches.cn: 两个义项解释了为什么这个词既能「还」，也能「感到」。

branches.en: The second sense lasts longer, because it has no final payment.
branches.cn: 第二个义项更长久，因为它没有最后一次结清。

intro.en: Debt forms a compact family around owing: the person who owes, the state of owing, and the relief of being free.
intro.cn: debt 这一族都围绕「欠」：欠的人、欠的状态，以及无债的轻松。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is debere, to owe; its participle debitum gives the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 debere（欠），其分词 debitum 演变成英语名词。

items.example: The debt was cleared last month.
items.exampleCN: 这笔债上个月结清了。

items.example: The debtor asked for more time.
items.exampleCN: 债务人请求宽限一些时间。

items.example: I am indebted to you for your help.
items.exampleCN: 你的帮助让我十分感激。

items.example: They were debt-free by forty.
items.exampleCN: 他们四十岁时已无债一身轻。

items.example: A debtless farmer sleeps well.
items.exampleCN: 不欠债的农夫睡得踏实。

items.meaning: a situation where debts cannot be paid
items.example: The country faced a debt crisis.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家面临债务危机。

items.meaning: the cancelling or easing of debts
items.example: The bank offered debt relief to farmers.
items.exampleCN: 银行给农民提供了债务减免。

items.meaning: a person paid to recover debts
items.example: A debt collector called twice.
items.exampleCN: 讨债人打了两次电话。

definition_en: a period of ten years
core_image: 日历上翻过的十本厚册
scene: 老照片记下了这个街区几十年的变化。The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
sceneCN: 这里 decade 指「十年」（第 1 个义项：十个年头）；句意是这家店在这个街角开了十年。

senses.title: Any period of ten years
senses.definition: a length of ten years counted from any starting point
senses.definitionCN: 从任意一点起算的十个年头
senses.example: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。
senses.why: Ten fingers, ten years: counting by tens is older than any calendar.
senses.whyCN: 十根手指、十个年头，按十计数比历法还要古老。

senses.title: A named ten-year span
senses.definition: one of the ten-year blocks used to talk about history
senses.definitionCN: 谈论历史时用来切分时间的一个十年段
senses.example: The music of that decade still sounds fresh.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年代的音乐如今听着仍然新鲜。
senses.why: History is easier to hold when it is cut into named blocks.
senses.whyCN: 历史切成有名字的块，才更容易被人握住。

intro.en: Decade came from Greek dekas, a group of ten, through Latin decas and French décade.
intro.cn: decade 经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade，上溯到希腊语 dekas（一组十个）。

items.en: Dekas meant a set of ten, from deka, the number ten.
items.cn: dekas 指一组十个，来自 deka（十）。

items.en: Decas kept the Greek sense of a group of ten things.
items.cn: decas 保留了希腊语「十个一组」的意思。

items.en: Décade was used for a period of ten days or ten years.
items.cn: décade 曾用来指十天或十年。

items.en: English settled decade on ten years.
items.cn: 英语把 decade 固定为「十年」。

items.en: The word now also labels cultural periods such as the nineties.
items.cn: 如今这个词也用来称呼九十年代这样的文化时期。

note.en: The look-alike group begins with the same dec- letters, and the meaning group measures time in different lengths.
note.cn: 形近组都以 dec- 开头，近义组则用不同长度来量时间。

entries.definition: to turn a code into ordinary language
a unit for measuring the loudness of sound
a flat shape with ten straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 有十条直边的平面图形

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years
a long period with a shared character
entries.definitionCN: 具有共同特征的漫长时期

entries.definition: the length of time something lasts

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with ten fingers and end with a block of history that has a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从十根手指开始，落到一段有了名字的历史。

normal.en: A decade is long enough to change a street and short enough to remember.
normal.cn: 十年长到能改一条街，又短到还记得清。

normal.en: Count ten new years and a decade has passed without a sound.
normal.cn: 数过十个新年，十年就悄没声地过去了。

normal.en: Photographs are the only scales that weigh a decade.
normal.cn: 照片是唯一能称出十年重量的秤。

normal.en: A child of one decade becomes the parent of the next.
normal.cn: 这个十年的孩子，成了下个十年的父母。

normal.en: Dec- at the front means ten, as in ten-sided shapes and ten-year spans.
normal.cn: 开头的 dec- 表示十，十边形和十年都是它。

abstract.en: Picture ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
abstract.cn: 想象十本厚日历堆在一个角落。

abstract.en: Picture the same corner photographed once every ten years.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个街角,每十年被拍下一次。

abstract.en: Picture a child and then the same face with grey hair.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子，然后是同一张脸生出白发。

examples.en: The shop has stood on this corner for a decade.
examples.cn: 这家店在这个街角已经开了十年。

examples.en: Prices have doubled over the past decade.
examples.cn: 过去十年里物价翻了一倍。

examples.en: Each decade of his life brought a new city.
examples.cn: 他人生中的每一个十年都带来一座新城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decade 记成「得开的」：de 加 cade 像「得开的」，十年一过，旧日子就得让开，新的日子开进来。

root: 源自希腊语 dekas（一组十个），经拉丁语 decas 与法语 décade 进入英语。法语里它一度兼指十天与十年，十七世纪英语才把它固定为十年，现代又用来指称九十年代这样有共同风格的历史时段。

sensesIntro.en: From any count of ten years to a block of history that carries a name.
sensesIntro.cn: 从任意的十个年头，到一段有了名字的历史。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ten thick calendars stacked in one corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：十本厚厚的日历堆在角落里。

branches.en: The first sense is a plain count of ten years from any point.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是从任意一点数满十年。

branches.en: Once the ten years are shared by many, they become a named block.
branches.cn: 当这十年被许多人共同经历，就成了有名字的一段。

branches.en: The same length of time, one measured and one remembered.
branches.cn: 同样长的时间，一个用来量，一个用来回忆。

branches.en: Both senses depend on counting by tens, an old habit of the hand.
branches.cn: 两个义项都靠按十计数，那是手上传下来的老习惯。

branches.en: Naming a decade is a way of saying that a change was shared.
branches.cn: 给十年命名，其实是在说这场变化人人都经历过。

intro.en: Decade belongs to the dec- family, where the number ten is spelled into shapes, spans and measures.
intro.cn: decade 属于 dec- 这一族，数字十被写进形状、时段与度量里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decem, ten, with decimus for tenth; Greek deka gave the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decem（十），decimus 表示第十；希腊语 deka 意思相同。

items.example: A decade passed before they met again.
items.exampleCN: 过了十年他们才又见面。

items.example: The report studies decadal change.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告研究十年尺度的变化。

items.example: The decennial census begins in spring.
items.exampleCN: 每十年一次的人口普查春天开始。

items.example: They finished a decade-long study.
items.exampleCN: 他们完成了一项长达十年的研究。

items.example: The project took a half-decade.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目花了五年。

items.example: A decades-old tree shades the yard.
items.exampleCN: 一棵几十年的老树遮着院子。

items.meaning: a formal word for ten years
items.example: The charter is renewed each decennium.
items.exampleCN: 这份章程每十年续签一次。

items.example: The map changed decade by decade.
items.exampleCN: 地图十年十年地变着。

latinEntries.example: Decem is the Latin word for ten.
Decimus marks the tenth place in a list.
latinEntries.exampleCN: decimus 表示列表中的第十位。

definition_en: of a good enough standard; honest and kind
core_image: 一件洗得干净、不新却合身的衬衫
scene: 他穿着干净的旧衬衫去面试，看着让人放心。He is a decent man who keeps his word.
sceneCN: 这里 decent 指「正派的」（第 3 个义项：为人端正）；句意他是个守信的正派人。

senses.title: Good enough in quality
senses.definition: acceptable in quality, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 质量可以接受，虽不算出色
senses.example: He finally found a decent job near home.
senses.exampleCN: 他终于在离家不远的地方找到一份像样的工作。
senses.why: A low bar is still a bar; decent marks the line above it.
senses.whyCN: 低的标准也是标准，decent 指的就是这条线以上。

senses.title: Proper and respectable
senses.definition: following accepted standards of dress or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 符合大家认可的穿着与举止标准
senses.example: Wear something decent to the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试时穿得体面一点。
senses.why: What is proper is decided by the eyes of other people.
senses.whyCN: 什么叫得体，是由别人的眼睛定的。

senses.title: Honest and kind
senses.definition: having good moral qualities
senses.definitionCN: 具备良好的品德
senses.example: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个守信的正派人。
senses.why: The word turns from manners to morals without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从礼貌转到品行，外形一点没变。

intro.en: Decent came from Latin decens, fitting or becoming, from decere, to be proper.
intro.cn: decent 来自拉丁语 decens（合适的、相称的），源于 decere（应当、合宜）。

items.en: Decere meant to be fitting or proper for someone.
items.cn: decere 指对某人来说是合宜的。

items.en: Decens described what suits a person's place and duty.
items.cn: decens 形容与身份和职责相称的东西。

items.en: Décent carried the sense of proper and modest.
items.cn: décent 带着得体、有分寸的意思。

items.en: Decent named behaviour that met the standards of the day.
items.cn: decent 指符合当时标准的行为。

items.en: It softened into good enough, as in a decent meal.
items.cn: 后来它软化成「过得去」，比如一顿还不错的饭。

note.en: The look-alike group sounds close but means something else, and the meaning group runs from proper to merely acceptable.
note.cn: 形近组听着相近却另有意思，近义组则从得体走到勉强可以。

entries.definition: a movement downward
happening a short time ago
to pour liquid into another container
entries.definitionCN: 把液体倒进另一个容器

entries.definition: considered proper by other people
correct for the situation
not too large or showy

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a clean old shirt and end with the quiet honesty behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一件干净的旧衬衫开始，落到衬衫背后的那份老实。

normal.en: A decent shirt is not new; it is clean and fits.
normal.cn: 体面的衬衫不必新，干净合身就行。

normal.en: Decent is the word for the middle, where most of life happens.
normal.cn: decent 是给中间地带用的词，而生活大多在那儿。

normal.en: Pay a decent wage and the work becomes decent too.
normal.cn: 给一份说得过去的工钱，活儿也跟着像样了。

normal.en: A decent man does the right thing when nobody is watching.
normal.cn: 正派的人，在没人看着时也做该做的事。

normal.en: One letter turns decent into descent, and the meaning falls away.
normal.cn: 换一个字母，decent 就成了 descent，意思一落千丈。

abstract.en: Picture a shirt ironed on a kitchen table.
abstract.cn: 想象一件在厨房桌上被熨平的衬衫。

abstract.en: Picture a meal that is plain, warm and enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿简单、热乎、吃得饱的饭。

abstract.en: Picture a man returning money he was never asked about.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把没人追问的钱还了回去。

examples.en: He is a decent man who keeps his word.
examples.cn: 他是个守信的正派人。

examples.en: She earns a decent salary and saves a little each month.
examples.cn: 她挣着一份不错的工资，每月还能存下一点。

examples.en: It was decent of you to wait for me.
examples.cn: 你等着我，真是厚道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decent 记成「得体身」：de 是得，cent 听起来像「身」，衣着得体、为人端正，就是得体身。

root: 来自拉丁语 decens（合宜的），源于 decere（应当如此），本义是「与身份相称」。经法语 décent 进入英语后先指合乎礼俗的举止，后来语气变软，日常里常表示「还过得去、像样」。

sensesIntro.en: From something acceptable, to something proper in others' eyes, to a person worth trusting.
sensesIntro.cn: 从还算可以的东西，到别人眼里得体的样子，再到值得信任的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clean, plain shirt that fits exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件干净朴素、正好合身的衬衫。

branches.en: The first sense only asks that a thing be acceptable.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只要求东西过得去。

branches.en: The second sense adds the eyes of other people.
branches.cn: 第二个义项添上了旁人的目光。

branches.en: The third moves from appearance to the person behind it.
branches.cn: 第三个义项从外表走到了外表背后的那个人。

branches.en: Quality and propriety both rest on a shared minimum.
branches.cn: 质量和得体，都靠一条大家公认的底线。

branches.en: Good manners and good morals are neighbours in this word.
branches.cn: 在这个词里，礼貌与品德是邻居。

intro.en: Decent pairs with its negative and its noun: decency, indecent, indecency.
intro.cn: decent 与否定形式和名词配对：decency、indecent、indecency。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is decere, to be fitting; decus gave the related idea of honour.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 decere（合宜），decus 则带来「荣誉、体面」的意思。

items.example: They live in a decent flat.
items.exampleCN: 他们住在一套还不错的公寓里。

items.example: He had the decency to apologise.
items.exampleCN: 他还有道歉的体面。

items.example: The room was decently furnished.
items.exampleCN: 房间布置得还算像样。

items.example: The sign was removed as indecent.
items.exampleCN: 那块招牌因不雅被拆掉了。

items.example: The court heard a charge of indecency.
items.exampleCN: 法庭审理了一项猥亵指控。

items.example: He was indecently dressed for the ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 他穿得不宜出席那个仪式。

items.example: They found a decent-looking hotel.
items.exampleCN: 他们找到一家看上去还像样的旅馆。

items.example: The flat has a decent-sized kitchen.
items.exampleCN: 这套公寓有个相当大的厨房。

latinEntries.example: Decere lies behind decent and decorum.

definition_en: to choose something after thinking about it
core_image: 岔路口上抬起又落下的一只脚
scene: 她在两个方案之间想了很久，终于抬脚走向其中一个。She decided to take the smaller office.
sceneCN: 这里 decide 指「决定」（第 1 个义项：考虑后作出选择）；句意是她决定要那间小一点的办公室。

senses.title: Choose after thinking
senses.definition: to make a choice after weighing the possibilities
senses.definitionCN: 权衡各种可能之后作出选择
senses.example: She decided to take the smaller office.
senses.exampleCN: 她决定要那间小一点的办公室。
senses.why: A choice becomes a decision when the mind stops weighing.
senses.whyCN: 当一个念头不再掂量，选择就成了决定。

senses.title: Settle a question
senses.definition: to give a judgement that ends a doubt or a case
senses.definitionCN: 作出终止疑问或案件的判断
senses.example: The judge decided the case in one morning.
senses.exampleCN: 法官用一上午就把案子判了。
senses.why: Someone must cut the argument, or it never ends.
senses.whyCN: 总得有人把争论切开，否则它永远不会结束。

senses.title: Fix the result
senses.definition: to be the thing that determines an outcome
senses.definitionCN: 成为决定最终结果的那个因素
senses.example: One goal decided the match.
senses.exampleCN: 一个进球决定了这场比赛。
senses.why: The last small event can carry the whole result.
senses.whyCN: 最后一个小事件，能扛起整个结果。

intro.en: Decide came from Latin decidere, to cut off, from de- and caedere, to cut.
intro.cn: decide 来自拉丁语 decidere（切断），由 de- 与 caedere（切）构成。

items.en: Decidere meant to cut off or cut through.
items.cn: decidere 指切下或切开。

items.en: Cutting a knot became a way of settling a question.
items.cn: 把结切开，成了了结疑问的办法。

items.en: Décider carried the sense of ending a doubt.
items.cn: décider 带着终结疑问的意思。

items.en: Decide entered English as a verb of judgement.
items.cn: decide 作为表示判断的动词进入英语。

items.en: The everyday sense is simply to choose.
items.cn: 如今最常见的用法就是「选」。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the -ide ending, and the meaning group moves from choosing to settling.
note.cn: 形近组都收在 -ide 上，近义组则从选择走到了断。

entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途造出的装置

to pick one out of several

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot at a fork and end with one goal that settles a whole match.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从岔路口的一只脚开始，落到一个定下整场比赛的进球。

normal.en: A decision is a cut; before it, both roads are still open.
normal.cn: 决定就是一刀切下去，切之前两条路都还开着。

normal.en: Thinking chooses nothing until the foot moves.
normal.cn: 脚不动，想再多也等于没选。

normal.en: Judges decide by cutting, not by adding.
normal.cn: 法官靠切开，而不是靠添加来判案。

normal.en: The last goal decides the match, but the first ten set it up.
normal.cn: 最后那个球决定了比赛，前十个球铺好了路。

normal.en: De- apart, -cide cut: to decide is to cut away one option.
normal.cn: de 是分开，cide 是切，决定就是把一个选项切掉。

abstract.en: Picture two paths and one lifted foot.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路和一只抬起的脚。

abstract.en: Picture a knife laid on a knotted string.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刀架在一个打了结的绳子上。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard changing by one number.
abstract.cn: 想象记分牌只变了一个数字。

examples.en: She decided to take the smaller office.
examples.cn: 她决定要那间小一点的办公室。

examples.en: We still have to decide where to meet.
examples.cn: 我们还得定下在哪里见面。

examples.en: The final point decided the game.
examples.cn: 最后一分决定了这场比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decide 记成「得塞的」：de 是得，cide 像「塞的」，心里塞满了选项，最后总得塞定一个。

root: 源自拉丁语 decidere，本义是「切断」，由 de（离开）与 caedere（切）组成。切断绳结的画面后来引申为「了结疑问、作出裁决」，再泛化为日常说的「拿定主意」。

sensesIntro.en: From cutting off one option, to cutting a case short, to one event cutting a result into place.
sensesIntro.cn: 从切掉一个选项，到把案件切断，再到一个事件把结果定死。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot lifted at a fork, about to fall on one path.
core.cn: 核心意象：岔路口抬起的一只脚，即将落在其中一条路上。

branches.en: The first sense is a private choice made by one person.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个人私下作出的选择。

branches.en: The second sense is a public cut made by someone with authority.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是有权之人当众切下的一刀。

branches.en: The third sense is an event that cuts the result into place.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一个事件把结果切定下来。

branches.en: A choice and a ruling both end a state of doubt.
branches.cn: 选择和裁决，都在终结一种不确定。

branches.en: Authority and outcome both use the image of a clean cut.
branches.cn: 权威与结果，都借用了干净一刀的形象。

intro.en: Decide grows into decision, decisive and the state of being undecided.
intro.cn: decide 长出 decision、decisive，以及「尚未决定」的状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is caedere, to cut; the -cide ending also appears in suicide and homicide.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 caedere（切），-cide 这个结尾也出现在 suicide 和 homicide 里。

items.example: They decided to stay another night.
items.exampleCN: 他们决定再住一晚。

items.example: The decision was announced at noon.
items.exampleCN: 决定在中午公布。

items.example: She gave a decisive answer.
items.exampleCN: 她给了个果断的答复。

items.example: He acted decisively at once.
items.exampleCN: 他立刻果断地行动起来。

items.example: The question is still undecided.
items.exampleCN: 这个问题还没有定论。

items.meaning: a person or match that settles it
items.example: The third game was the decider.
items.exampleCN: 第三局是决胜局。

items.example: He was too indecisive to choose.
items.exampleCN: 他犹豫不决，挑不出来。

items.example: Her indecision cost them the chance.
items.exampleCN: 她的犹豫让他们错过了机会。

latinEntries.example: Caedere gives English decide and precise.
latinEntries.exampleCN: caedere 给英语带来 decide 和 precise。

definition_en: a choice that you make after thinking
core_image: 桌上盖了章的那页纸
scene: 会开到最后，大家举手通过了一个方案。The committee reached a decision before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 decision 指「决定」（第 1 个义项：考虑后作出的选择）；句意是委员会中午前作出了决定。

senses.title: A choice that is made
senses.definition: a judgement or choice reached after thought
senses.definitionCN: 经过思考后得出的判断或选择
senses.example: The committee reached a decision before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会中午之前作出了决定。
senses.why: A choice becomes a thing once it is spoken and written down.
senses.whyCN: 选择一旦被说出口、写下来，就成了一件东西。

senses.title: The ability to decide firmly
senses.definition: the quality of being able to choose quickly and firmly
senses.definitionCN: 能迅速而坚定地作出选择的能力
senses.example: She is known for her decision and clear speech.
senses.exampleCN: 她以果断和说话清楚出名。
senses.why: The same word names the act and the character behind it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指行为，也指行为背后的性格。

senses.title: An official ruling
senses.definition: a formal judgement given by a court or a public body
senses.definitionCN: 法院或公共机构给出的正式判断
senses.example: The court's decision was read aloud in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决在庭上被宣读。
senses.why: A public body must put its judgement in a form others can obey.
senses.whyCN: 公共机构得把判断写成别人能够遵从的形式。

intro.en: Decision is the Latin noun decisio, a cutting off, from decidere, to cut off.
intro.cn: decision 就是拉丁名词 decisio（切断），来自动词 decidere。

items.en: Decisio named the act of cutting something off.
items.cn: decisio 指把东西切下来的动作。

items.en: It came to mean the settling of a dispute.
items.cn: 后来指争端的了结。

items.en: Décision meant a judgement that ends doubt.
items.cn: décision 指终结疑问的判断。

items.en: Decision entered English as a formal ruling.
items.cn: decision 作为正式的裁定进入英语。

items.en: It now also covers small daily choices.
items.cn: 如今它也指日常里的小选择。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ision ending, and the meaning group runs from a plain choice to a formal verdict.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ision 结尾，近义组则从普通选择走到正式裁断。

entries.definition: the act of separating into parts
the quality of being exact
mockery and laughter at someone
an act of picking one thing
the decision of a court or jury
a formal decision by a group

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stamped page and end with the firmness behind a quick answer.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一页盖了章的文件开始，落到一个干脆答复背后的那股定力。

normal.en: A decision is a cut that leaves one road behind.
normal.cn: 决定是一刀切下去，把一条路留在身后。

normal.en: Talk is cheap until someone signs the page.
normal.cn: 没人签字之前，话说得再漂亮都不算数。

normal.en: The hardest decisions are the ones with two good answers.
normal.cn: 最难的决定，是两个答案都不错的那种。

normal.en: Decisiveness is speed borrowed from confidence.
normal.cn: 果断是从自信那里借来的速度。

normal.en: A court decision ends the argument but not the feelings.
normal.cn: 法庭的裁决结束了争论，却结束不了情绪。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a seal onto warm wax.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把印章按在温热的蜡上。

abstract.en: Picture a row of hands going up at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象一排手在同一刻举起。

abstract.en: Picture one page left on a table after everyone has gone.
abstract.cn: 想象人都走了，桌上只留一页纸。

examples.en: The committee reached a decision before noon.
examples.cn: 委员会中午之前作出了决定。

examples.en: Moving abroad was the hardest decision of her life.
examples.cn: 搬去国外是她一生中最难的决定。

examples.en: The court's decision surprised both sides.
examples.cn: 法院的裁决让双方都感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decision 记成「得细想」：de 是得，cision 像「细想」，一件事得细想清楚，才拿得出决定。

root: 来自拉丁名词 decisio（切断），源头是 decidere（切下）。切断绳结的画面先引申为争端的了结与正式裁定，十五世纪进入英语，后来语气放宽，日常小事上的选择也叫 decision。

sensesIntro.en: From a choice put into words, to the firmness that produced it, to a ruling others must obey.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被说成话的选择，到产生它的那份定力，再到别人必须遵从的裁断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamped page lying on a table after the meeting.
core.cn: 核心意象：散会后桌上放着那页盖了章的文件。

branches.en: The first sense is the choice itself, now fixed in words.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是选择本身，此刻已被话固定住。

branches.en: The second sense is the inner firmness that makes such choices possible.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是让这种选择成为可能的内在定力。

branches.en: The third sense is the version a public body must hand down.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是公共机构必须下达的那种版本。

branches.en: A private choice and a public ruling share one written form.
branches.cn: 私人选择和公开裁决，共用一种书面形式。

branches.en: Without firmness, a choice never becomes a thing.
branches.cn: 没有定力，选择永远成不了一件东西。

intro.en: Decision holds the -ion noun of the -cide family: decide, decisive, indecision.
intro.cn: decision 是 -cide 一族里的名词形式，同族还有 decide、decisive、indecision。

latinIntro.en: The stem is caedere, to cut, giving cis- in decision and precise.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 caedere（切），在 decision、precise 里写作 cis-。

items.example: The decision took three hours.
items.exampleCN: 这个决定花了三个小时。

items.example: It was a decisive moment.
items.exampleCN: 那是个决定性的时刻。

items.example: They voted decisively against it.
items.exampleCN: 他们果断地投票反对。

items.example: Her decisiveness saved the day.
items.exampleCN: 她的果断扭转了局面。

items.example: Indecision delayed the plan.
items.exampleCN: 犹豫不决拖慢了计划。

items.meaning: not able to settle a matter
items.example: An indecisive leader wastes time.
items.exampleCN: 优柔寡断的领导者浪费时间。

items.example: The team improved its decision-making.
items.exampleCN: 这个团队改进了决策方式。

items.example: The decision maker was not in the room.
items.exampleCN: 决策者当时不在房间里。

definition_en: to say something officially or firmly
core_image: 一个人举起手，向所有人说明一件事
scene: 主席敲了敲桌子，当众说明会议开始。The chair declared the meeting open.
sceneCN: 这里 declare 指「宣布」（第 1 个义项：正式公开地说）；句意是主席宣布会议开始。

senses.title: Announce officially
senses.definition: to state something openly in an official way
senses.definitionCN: 以官方的方式公开说明某事
senses.example: The chair declared the meeting open.
senses.exampleCN: 主席宣布会议开始。
senses.why: An official voice turns a private fact into a public one.
senses.whyCN: 官方的声音把私事变成了众人皆知的事。

senses.title: Say firmly
senses.definition: to state a belief with confidence
senses.definitionCN: 很有把握地说出自己的看法
senses.example: She declared that the plan would work.
senses.exampleCN: 她断言这个计划行得通。
senses.why: The word lends a plain sentence the weight of a promise.
senses.whyCN: 这个词给一句普通的话添上了承诺的分量。

senses.title: Report goods to customs
senses.definition: to list goods or money to officials
senses.definitionCN: 向官员列出所带的物品或钱款
senses.example: You must declare any cash over the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 超过限额的现金必须申报。
senses.why: What is hidden must be named before it may pass.
senses.whyCN: 藏着的东西，得先被说出来才能通过。

intro.en: Declare came from Latin declarare, to make clear, from clarus, bright.
intro.cn: declare 来自拉丁语 declarare（使清楚），源于 clarus（明亮的）。

items.en: Clarus meant bright, plain and easy to see.
items.cn: clarus 指明亮的、平白易见的。

items.en: Declarare meant to make a matter bright for all to see.
items.cn: declarare 指把事情照亮，让所有人看见。

items.en: Declarer meant to announce or explain openly.
items.cn: declarer 指公开宣布或解释。

items.en: Declare entered English with the sense of making clear.
items.cn: declare 进入英语时，意思是「说清楚」。

items.en: The customs sense grew from the same idea of naming openly.
items.cn: 海关用法也从「公开说出」这个意思长出来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the opening and closing sounds, and the meaning group runs from telling to proclaiming.
note.cn: 形近组首尾音相近，近义组则从告知走到宣告。

entries.definition: to speak in a loud, formal way
entries.definitionCN: 以响亮正式的方式讲话

entries.definition: to become smaller or to refuse

to say something clearly and formally

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a gavel on a table and end with a bag opened at a customs desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从敲在桌上的小锤开始，落到海关柜台上打开的一只包。

normal.en: To declare is to switch the light on a fact.
normal.cn: declare 就是给一件事实开灯。

normal.en: The chair says three words and the meeting exists.
normal.cn: 主席说三个词，会议才真正开始。

normal.en: What you declare, you can no longer deny.
normal.cn: 你宣布过的事，就再也否认不了。

normal.en: A customs bag is honest only when it is opened.
normal.cn: 海关的包，只有打开时才诚实。

normal.en: Clarus meant bright, and declare still means to bring into the light.
normal.cn: clarus 本指明亮，declare 至今仍是把东西拿到光下。

abstract.en: Picture a gavel coming down once.
abstract.cn: 想象小锤落下一次。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised before a crowd begins to listen.
abstract.cn: 想象人群开始听之前，一只手举了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a bag unzipped under a bright lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一只包在亮灯下被拉开。

examples.en: The chair declared the meeting open.
examples.cn: 主席宣布会议开始。

examples.en: They declared independence in the summer of that year.
examples.cn: 那年夏天他们宣布独立。

examples.en: I have nothing to declare.
examples.cn: 我没有需要申报的东西。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 declare 记成「得客来而」：de 是得，clare 听着像「客来而」，客人一到，主人得当众说一声欢迎。

root: 来自拉丁语 declarare（使清楚），根子是 clarus（明亮的）。十四世纪进入英语时意为「说明、讲清」，后来用于官方场合表示公开宣布，又延伸到向海关如实说明所带物品。

sensesIntro.en: From an official word that starts a meeting, to a firm belief, to goods named at a border.
sensesIntro.cn: 从让会议开始的那句官方话，到坚定的看法，再到在关口说清的物品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a raised hand making one fact public.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手举起，把一件事变成公开的。

branches.en: The first sense is the official voice that changes a situation.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是改变局面的那声官方宣布。

branches.en: The second sense is a person speaking with full confidence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人满有把握地说话。

branches.en: The third sense is the same act performed for the state.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是同一个动作，只是对国家做。

branches.en: A meeting and a border both wait for someone to speak first.
branches.cn: 会议和关口，都在等一个人先开口。

branches.en: Firmness and honesty are the same tone in different rooms.
branches.cn: 坚定和如实，是不同场合里的同一种语气。

intro.en: Declare and its noun declaration carry the whole clar- family of clearness.
intro.cn: declare 及其名词 declaration 带着整个 clar- 家族，都与「清楚」有关。

latinIntro.en: The root is clarus, bright; clarare meant to make bright.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 clarus（明亮），clarare 意为使明亮。

items.example: They declared the winner at once.
items.exampleCN: 他们立刻宣布了获胜者。

items.example: The declaration was signed by all.
items.exampleCN: 宣言由所有人签署。

items.example: A declarative sentence ends with a full stop.
items.exampleCN: 陈述句以句号结尾。

items.example: The ruling was declaratory only.
items.exampleCN: 那项裁定只是宣告性质的。

items.example: The declarer must show a passport.
items.exampleCN: 申报者必须出示护照。

items.example: Their declared goal is zero waste.
items.exampleCN: 他们公开的目标是零浪费。

items.example: Undeclared income must be taxed.
items.exampleCN: 未申报的收入必须纳税。

items.meaning: to announce a state of war
items.example: The country declared war at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 这个国家在黎明时宣战。

definition_en: to become smaller or weaker; to refuse politely
core_image: 一条缓缓下滑的曲线
scene: 入冬后游客少了，街上的小店一间间关了门。Sales declined sharply after the summer.
sceneCN: 这里 decline 指「下降」（第 1 个义项：数量变少）；句意是夏天过后销量急剧下滑。

senses.title: Become less in number
senses.definition: to fall in number, amount or strength
senses.definitionCN: 数量、数额或力量变小
senses.example: Sales declined sharply after the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天过后销量急剧下滑。
senses.why: A line that turns downward is the plainest sign of loss.
senses.whyCN: 曲线往下一拐，是最直白的损失信号。

senses.title: Refuse politely
senses.definition: to say no to an offer in a courteous way
senses.definitionCN: 有礼貌地回绝别人的提议
senses.example: She declined the invitation with a short note.
senses.exampleCN: 她写了一封短笺婉拒了邀请。
senses.why: To bend away from a request is gentler than to reject it.
senses.whyCN: 从请求旁边弯开去，比直接推开要温和。

senses.title: A slow loss of strength
senses.definition: a gradual weakening of health, power or quality
senses.definitionCN: 健康、实力或品质逐渐变弱
senses.example: The town's decline began when the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场关闭后，这座小镇开始衰落。
senses.why: Small losses, repeated, become a state you can name.
senses.whyCN: 细小的损失反复发生，就成了可以命名的一种状态。

intro.en: Decline came from Latin declinare, to bend away, from clinare, to bend.
intro.cn: decline 来自拉丁语 declinare（弯开），源于 clinare（弯曲）。

items.en: Clinare meant to bend or lean.
items.cn: clinare 指弯曲或倾斜。

items.en: Declinare meant to bend away from a straight line.
items.cn: declinare 指偏离直线弯向一边。

items.en: Decliner covered both sinking and turning aside.
items.cn: decliner 既指下沉，也指让到一边。

items.en: Decline entered English for falling numbers and refused offers.
items.cn: decline 进入英语时兼指数字下滑与拒绝提议。

items.en: Grammar kept a third sense, the bending of word forms.
items.cn: 语法保留了第三个义项，即词形的屈折变化。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -cline shape, and the meaning group moves from falling to refusing.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -cline 的形状，近义组则从下跌走到拒绝。

entries.definition: to lean or tend towards something
entries.definitionCN: 向某处倾斜或有某种倾向

entries.definition: to lie back in a relaxed way
to speak in a loud formal manner
entries.definitionCN: 以响亮正式的方式讲话

entries.definition: to become or make smaller
to say that you will not do something
to become or make less strong

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line bending down and end with an offer gently put aside.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条向下弯的线开始，落到被轻轻放到一边的提议。

normal.en: Decline is a curve, not a cliff.
normal.cn: decline 是条曲线，不是悬崖。

normal.en: A polite no is also a way of stepping aside.
normal.cn: 礼貌的拒绝，也是一种让开。

normal.en: Towns decline one closed shop at a time.
normal.cn: 小镇是一间店一间店地衰落的。

normal.en: The same bending away that refuses an offer also lowers a number.
normal.cn: 把提议绕开的那一弯，也把数字压了下去。

normal.en: Grammar declines nouns the way a road declines a hill.
normal.cn: 语法让名词变格，就像道路顺坡而下。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil line easing down a page.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔线在纸上缓缓下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to say no thanks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起来表示谢绝。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window with paper over the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇玻璃上糊了纸的店窗。

examples.en: Sales declined sharply after the summer.
examples.cn: 夏天过后销量急剧下滑。

examples.en: She declined the invitation with a short note.
examples.cn: 她写了一封短笺婉拒了邀请。

examples.en: The industry is in decline and few young people join it.
examples.cn: 这个行业正在衰退，很少有年轻人入行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decline 记成「低可赖」：de 是低，cline 像「靠」，坡一低，人就只能靠着往下溜。

root: 源自拉丁语 declinare（弯开、偏斜），词根 clinare 意为弯曲。它的两个主要意思都从「弯」来：数字往下弯是下降，人往旁边弯是婉拒；语法上的变格用法也沿用同一个比喻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line bending downward, to an offer bent aside, to a long state of weakening.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向下弯的线，到被让开的提议，再到长期变弱的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line easing gently downward across a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线在纸页上缓缓向下。

branches.en: The first sense is quantity dropping on a chart.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是图表上的数量往下掉。

branches.en: The second sense is a person stepping politely aside.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人礼貌地让到一边。

branches.en: The third sense is a long slope that no single fall explains.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一道慢坡，单次下跌解释不了。

branches.en: A small fall repeated becomes a long decline.
branches.cn: 一次小跌反复发生，就成了长期衰退。

branches.en: To decline an offer is to let it fall away from you.
branches.cn: 婉拒一个提议，就是让它从身边落下去。

intro.en: Decline holds the -clin- stem, shared with incline, recline and declination.
intro.cn: decline 带着 -clin- 词干，与 incline、recline、declination 同族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is clinare, to bend; Greek had a related word for a bed, kline.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 clinare（弯曲），希腊语里表示床的 kline 与之同源。

items.example: Profits declined for three years.
items.exampleCN: 利润连续三年下降。

items.example: The declining birth rate worried them.
items.exampleCN: 下降的出生率让他们担心。

items.example: The compass shows magnetic declination.
items.exampleCN: 罗盘显示出磁偏角。

items.example: Latin declension follows clear patterns.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语变格遵循清楚的规律。

items.example: The noun is indeclinable.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词没有词形变化。

items.meaning: to turn an offer down politely
items.example: He declined the offer with thanks.
items.exampleCN: 他道谢后谢绝了提议。

items.example: The chart shows a sharp decline.
items.exampleCN: 图表显示出急剧下降。

items.example: Demand for coal is on the decline.
items.exampleCN: 煤炭需求正在下滑。

latinEntries.example: Clinare gives English decline and incline.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clinare 给英语带来 decline 和 incline。

definition_en: going a long way down from the top or the surface
core_image: 从井口往下望，看不见底
scene: 井口往下望，黑洞洞的，看不到底。The well is deep and cold.
sceneCN: 这里 deep 指「深的」（第 1 个义项：从上往下距离大）；句意是这口井又深又冷。

senses.title: Far from top to bottom
senses.definition: reaching a long way down from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面向下的距离很长
senses.example: The well is deep and cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这口井又深又冷。
senses.why: Distance downward is the first thing the eye cannot measure.
senses.whyCN: 往下的距离，是眼睛最先量不出来的东西。

senses.title: Strong and serious
senses.definition: intense, serious, or felt with great force
senses.definitionCN: 强烈、严肃或感受极重的
senses.example: She fell into a deep sleep after the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 旅途之后她沉沉睡去。
senses.why: What goes far down inside a person is also called deep.
senses.whyCN: 一个人内里沉得很深的东西，也叫 deep。

senses.title: The deepest part
senses.definition: the part of something furthest from the surface
senses.definitionCN: 某物离表面最远的那一部分
senses.example: Strange fish live in the deep.
senses.exampleCN: 奇怪的鱼生活在深处。
senses.why: A place that is far down can be named as a place.
senses.whyCN: 离表面很远的地方，可以当成一个地点来称呼。

intro.en: Deep is an Old English word, deop, from a Germanic root meaning hollow and far down.
intro.cn: deep 是古英语词 deop，来自一个意为「中空、深陷」的日耳曼词根。

items.en: The root named what lies far below the surface.
items.cn: 这个词根指位于表面之下很远的地方。

items.en: Deop described wells, water and valleys.
items.cn: deop 形容井、水与山谷。

items.en: The word moved from ground to feeling and thought.
items.cn: 这个词从地面挪到了情感与思想上。

items.en: Deep colours and deep sleep borrowed the idea of fullness.
items.cn: 深色与熟睡借用了「满而沉」的意思。

items.en: Deep now measures both space and intensity.
items.cn: 如今 deep 既量空间，也量强度。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter, and the meaning group moves from literal depth to intensity.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母，近义组则从实指的深走到抽象的重。

entries.definition: to consider something to be true
to put something quickly into liquid
an action that is done
very deep in feeling or thought
entries.definitionCN: 在感情或思想上极深的

entries.definition: having no bottom that can be reached
very strong in degree

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a well that has no visible bottom and end with a feeling that has no floor either.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一口望不到底的井开始，落到一份同样没有底的感情。

normal.en: A deep well and a deep grief are both measured by how long the echo takes.
normal.cn: 深井和深悲，都靠回声多久才回来来衡量。

normal.en: The surface tells you nothing; the rope tells you everything.
normal.cn: 表面什么也不说，绳子才说明一切。

normal.en: Deep sleep is a room with the lights off.
normal.cn: 熟睡是一间关了灯的房间。

normal.en: A deep voice comes from the chest, not the throat.
normal.cn: 低沉的声音来自胸腔，不来自喉咙。

normal.en: Depth is deep plus -th, the shape of the distance itself.
normal.cn: depth 是 deep 加 -th，正是那段距离本身的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a coin falling and no sound coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币落下去，却没有回声传回来。

abstract.en: Picture a diver's light fading into blue.
abstract.cn: 想象潜水员的灯光渐渐没入蓝色。

abstract.en: Picture a person quiet for a long time and then speaking one true sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人沉默很久，然后说出一句真话。

examples.en: The well is deep and cold.
examples.cn: 这口井又深又冷。

examples.en: He took a deep breath and began to speak.
examples.cn: 他深吸一口气，开口说话。

examples.en: The lake is deepest near the middle.
examples.cn: 湖中央一带最深。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deep 记成「地铺」：de 是地，ep 听着像「铺」，地铺一铺就很深，往下望不见底。

root: 源自古英语 deop，更早是日耳曼语词根，本义是「中空、深陷」。它先形容井、水与山谷，后来从地面挪到人身上，用来形容沉睡、颜色、感情与思想的浓重，抽象与具体始终共用同一个词。

sensesIntro.en: From distance below the surface, to intensity inside a person, to the far place itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 从表面之下的距离，到人内里的强烈，再到那个很远的地点本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: looking down a well and seeing no bottom.
core.cn: 核心意象：往井里望下去，看不到底。

branches.en: The first sense is plain distance from top to bottom.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是从上到下的距离。

branches.en: The second sense moves that distance inside a person or a colour.
branches.cn: 第二个义项把这段距离挪进了人心里或颜色里。

branches.en: The third sense turns the far-down place into a noun.
branches.cn: 第三个义项把那个很下面的地方变成了名词。

branches.en: Space and feeling share one image of going down.
branches.cn: 空间与情感，共用「往下走」这一幅画面。

branches.en: What is deep can also be visited as a place.
branches.cn: 深的东西，也能当成一个地方走进去。

intro.en: Deep grows into deeply, deepen, depth and a set of compounds about the sea and roots.
intro.cn: deep 长出 deeply、deepen、depth，以及一批与深海、深根有关的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in deep; Latin used altus and profundus for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: deep 里没有拉丁成分，拉丁语用 altus 和 profundus 表示同样的意思。

items.example: The water is deep here.
items.exampleCN: 这里的水很深。

items.example: She was deeply moved.
items.exampleCN: 她被深深打动了。

items.example: They deepened the channel last year.
items.exampleCN: 他们去年把水道挖深了。

items.example: The depth of the pool is two metres.
items.exampleCN: 泳池的深度是两米。

items.example: The deepness of the silence surprised him.
items.exampleCN: 那份沉默之深让他吃惊。

items.example: Deep-sea fish rarely come up.
items.exampleCN: 深海鱼很少浮上来。

items.example: It is a deep-rooted habit.
items.exampleCN: 这是个根深蒂固的习惯。

items.meaning: placed far back in the face
items.example: He has deep-set eyes.
items.exampleCN: 他有一双深陷的眼睛。

definition_en: far below a surface, or to a very great degree
core_image: 一颗石子沉进水里，一直落到看不见的深处
scene: 她把话说得很慢，眼睛看着桌角，像是从很里面取出来的。She was deeply moved by the letter.
sceneCN: 这里 deeply 指「深深地」（第 1 个义项：一直落到内部很深处）；句意是那封信让她深受触动。

senses.title: Far below the surface
senses.definition: at or towards a great distance below a surface
senses.definitionCN: 在表面以下很深的地方
senses.example: The anchor sank deeply into the soft mud.
senses.exampleCN: 锚深深地陷进软泥里。
senses.why: Depth is measured by how far a thing travels downward.
senses.whyCN: 深度就是看一样东西往下走了多远。

senses.title: To a very great degree
senses.definition: very much, used with feelings, needs and beliefs
senses.definitionCN: 非常，多与情感、需要和信念连用
senses.example: She was deeply moved by the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 那封信让她深受触动。
senses.why: A feeling that reaches the bottom of us cannot be called mild.
senses.whyCN: 一直落到心底的感受，就不能算轻微。

senses.title: In a thorough and serious way
senses.definition: in a careful and thorough manner, of thought or study
senses.definitionCN: 在思考或研究上认真而透彻
senses.example: He thought deeply before he gave his answer.
senses.exampleCN: 他深思之后才给出回答。
senses.why: Thinking that goes far down is thinking done well.
senses.whyCN: 想得够深，才算想得够好。

intro.en: Deeply is deep plus the old adverb ending -ly, and deep goes back to an Old English word for a low place.
intro.cn: deeply 是 deep 加古老的副词词尾 -ly；deep 则来自古英语中表示低处的词。

items.en: Deop named the sea and any hollow place that went far down.
items.cn: deop 指大海，也指任何往下很深的凹陷之处。

items.en: The adverb ending -lice was already shortening to -ly.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -lice 当时已经在缩成 -ly。

items.en: Writers used deeply for both sunken things and strong feelings.
items.cn: 作家用它同时写沉下去的东西和强烈的感情。

items.en: Deeply settled into phrases about grief, sleep and debt.
items.cn: 它稳稳进入描写悲伤、睡眠与债务的说法里。

items.en: Today it mostly measures the strength of a feeling or belief.
items.cn: 如今它多半用来衡量情感或信念的强度。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the deep root, and the meaning group offers stronger adverbs for the same feeling.
note.cn: 形近组共用同一个「深」的根，近义组则给出表示同一种感受的更强副词。

entries.definition: going a long way down from the top
the distance from the top to the bottom
to make or become deeper
in a way that touches the very bottom of feeling
entries.definitionCN: 以触及情感最深处的方式

entries.definition: with very strong force or feeling
entries.definitionCN: 带着极强的力量或情感

entries.definition: very much, often of respect or thanks
entries.definitionCN: 非常，常用于敬意或感谢

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a stone dropping into still water and end with a thought that goes all the way down.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一颗石子落进静水开始，落到一直想到底的心思。

normal.en: A stone is not loud when it lands; the quiet is how you know it went far.
normal.cn: 石子落水并不响，安静才说明它落得够深。

normal.en: Deep sleep and deep sorrow both take you where no one can follow.
normal.cn: 沉睡与深悲都会把你带到别人跟不进去的地方。

normal.en: When a letter makes your eyes hot, you have been moved deeply.
normal.cn: 一封信让眼睛发热，就是被深深打动了。

normal.en: Roots are never seen; that is why they hold the tree so well.
normal.cn: 根从来看不见，所以才把树抱得那么牢。

normal.en: Add -ly to deep and the depth turns into a manner of doing.
normal.cn: deep 后面加 -ly，深度就变成了一种做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching into dark water and not finding the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸进暗水里，怎么也摸不到底。

abstract.en: Picture a word spoken so low that the room leans in to hear it.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话说得极轻，整间屋子都凑过去听。

abstract.en: Picture roots under grass, wider than the branches above.
abstract.cn: 想象草下的根系，比上面的枝叶还要铺得开。

examples.en: We are deeply grateful for all the help you gave us.
examples.cn: 我们非常感激你给予的全部帮助。

examples.en: The well is deeply cut into the hard rock.
examples.cn: 这口井深深地凿进坚硬的岩石里。

examples.en: She breathed deeply and began to speak.
examples.cn: 她深深吸了一口气，开始讲话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 deeply 记成「底里」：deep 是深，ly 是「地」，一直到底里，就是深深地。

root: deep 源自古英语 deop，本义是「往下的深处」，可指海，也可指任何凹陷。加副词词尾 -ly 之后，deeply 同时继承了具体与抽象两层意思：既指沉在下面，也指情感、信念或思考达到最深处。

sensesIntro.en: From a stone going down, to a heart that is touched, to a mind that thinks it through.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一颗石子往下沉，到一颗心被打动，再到一个念头被想透。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone sinking until the bottom cannot be seen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗石子沉下去，直到看不见底。

branches.en: The first sense is simple distance downward, measured in space.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是往下的距离，用空间来量。

branches.en: The same downward movement, felt in the chest, becomes strong emotion.
branches.cn: 同样的往下，落到胸口，就成了强烈的情感。

branches.en: Applied to thought, depth means care taken to the end.
branches.cn: 用在思考上，深度就是一直做到最后的认真。

branches.en: Space and feeling share one word because both have a bottom.
branches.cn: 空间与情感共用一个词，因为两者都有底。

branches.en: A strong feeling and a deep thought are both things we do not skim.
branches.cn: 强烈的感受与深刻的思考，都是不能草草掠过的东西。

intro.en: Deeply belongs to the deep family: a verb of deepening, a noun of depth and a set of compounds.
intro.cn: deeply 属于 deep 这一族：有表示加深的动词、表示深度的名词，还有一批复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in deeply; both parts are native English.
latinIntro.cn: deeply 里没有拉丁成分，两个部分都是英语本族语。

items.meaning: in a deep or intense way
items.example: They talked deeply into the night.
items.exampleCN: 他们一直深谈到夜里。

items.example: The lake is deep in the middle.
items.exampleCN: 湖中央很深。

items.example: The river deepens after the bend.
items.exampleCN: 河流转过弯之后变深了。

items.meaning: the measure of how deep something is
items.example: They measured the depth of the pool.
items.exampleCN: 他们量了水池的深度。

items.example: The deepness of his voice filled the hall.
items.exampleCN: 他低沉的嗓音充满大厅。

items.meaning: firmly fixed and hard to change
items.example: It is a deep-seated habit.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个根深蒂固的习惯。

items.meaning: long established and hard to remove
items.example: The fear was deep-rooted in the village.
items.exampleCN: 这种恐惧在村里根深蒂固。

items.meaning: found in the far part of the sea
items.example: They study deep-water fish.
items.exampleCN: 他们研究深水鱼类。

definition_en: to win against an opponent, or to make a plan fail; also a loss in a contest
core_image: 对手低下头，慢慢走出场地
scene: 终场哨响，主队球员垂着头走向更衣室，看台上没有一个人说话。The young team defeated the champions by one goal.
sceneCN: 这里 defeat 指「击败」（第 1 个义项：在比赛或争斗中战胜对手）；句意是这支年轻队伍以一球之差战胜了冠军队。

senses.title: Win a contest against someone
senses.definition: to win a victory over an opponent in a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中战胜对手
senses.example: Our team defeated the visitors by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队以两球战胜了客队。
senses.why: A contest ends the moment one side can no longer answer.
senses.whyCN: 比赛在一方再也还不了手的那一刻就结束了。

senses.title: Make a hope or plan fail
senses.definition: to cause a plan, hope or purpose to come to nothing
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、希望或目的无法实现
senses.example: The heavy rain defeated our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨让我们的野餐计划落空了。
senses.why: A plan can be beaten just as a person can be beaten.
senses.whyCN: 计划也会像人一样被打败。

senses.title: A loss in a contest
senses.definition: the fact of losing a game, battle or election
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或选举中输掉的事实
senses.example: The defeat left the players silent in the changing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失败让球员们在更衣室里一言不发。
senses.why: Every victory leaves behind a second word for the other side.

intro.en: Defeat came to English through French, but its pieces are Latin: dis- meaning apart and facere meaning to do.

items.en: English took the word as a noun for a lost battle.

items.en: The verb grew beside the noun and took over the action.

items.en: A team can defeat a rival, and a problem can defeat a plan.

root: 来自拉丁语 disfacere，由 dis-（分开）与 facere（做）组成，本义是把做好的东西拆掉、毁掉；经古法语 desfait 进入英语。它先指打输一场仗的结果，十六世纪起动词用法兴盛，后来又引申为让计划、希望落空。

sensesIntro.en: From a rival who cannot answer, to a plan that cannot happen, to the word for losing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从再也还不了手的对手，到无法实现的计划，再到表示输掉的那个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one side walks off the field with a lowered head.

branches.en: The first sense is a rival who can no longer answer.

branches.en: The same force applied to a plan leaves it undone.

branches.en: Seen from the other side, the same event is called a loss.

branches.en: One word serves both winner and loser, depending on who speaks.

branches.en: Both senses describe something that stopped before it finished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没走完就停下来的事。

intro.en: Defeat grows a small family of nouns about giving up and adjectives about never being beaten.

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is facere, to do, with the prefix dis- meaning apart.

senses.title: Guarding against attack

senses.title: The forces and works of a country

intro.en: Defence goes back to Latin defendere, to ward off, built from de- away and -fendere to strike.
intro.cn: defence 上溯到拉丁语 defendere（挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）组成。

items.en: Defendere meant to push a blow away from oneself.
items.cn: defendere 意为把打来的一击推开。

items.en: Defense carried the word into the language of law and war.
items.cn: defense 把这个词带进法律与战争的语言。

items.en: English used defence for both a shield and a plea.
items.cn: 英语用它同时指盾牌和申辩。

items.en: Spelling split, with defence in Britain and defense in America.
items.cn: 拼写分成两支，英国用 defence，美国用 defense。

items.en: Defence now also names a whole national system of protection.
items.cn: 如今它还可以指整套国家防护体系。

root: 源自拉丁语 defendere（把打击挡开），由 de-（离开）与 -fendere（击打）合成，经古法语 defense 进入英语。它最早兼指盾牌与申辩，十七世纪后英式拼作 defence、美式拼作 defense，如今还引申为整个国家的防务体系。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall that holds, to a voice that answers in court, to a system that guards a country.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate shut with a shield behind it.

intro.en: Defence gathers verbs, adjectives and nouns about guarding and about speaking up.

senses.title: Keep someone safe from attack
senses.definition: to protect a person or place from harm or attack

senses.example: Two soldiers defended the bridge all night.

senses.title: Hold a position in sport

senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止对方得分或夺走头衔
