senses.title: Be the mark of a character
senses.definition: to be the quality that clearly marks a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 成为清楚标示人或事物特点的品质
senses.example: Patience defines a good teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。
senses.why: The line around a thing is what lets us know it again.
senses.whyCN: 把一样东西圈起来的那条线，让我们能再认出它。

intro.en: Define comes from Latin definire, to set a boundary, from de- completely and finis end or limit.
intro.cn: define 来自拉丁语 definire（划定界限），由 de-（彻底）与 finis（终点、界限）组成。

items.en: Finis meant a boundary, the end of a field or of a life.
items.cn: finis 指边界，可以是一块田的尽头，也可以是生命的终点。

items.en: Definire meant to draw the line around a thing.
items.cn: definire 意为绕着一件事物画出界线。

items.en: Definir kept the sense of settling and deciding.
items.cn: definir 保留了确定与裁定的意思。

items.en: English used define for explaining words as well as limits.
items.cn: 英语用它既讲界限，也讲词义。

items.en: Today we define terms, borders, duties and even a style.
items.cn: 如今我们定义术语、边界、职责，甚至一种风格。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fine ending, and the meaning group moves from naming to making plain.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fine 这个尾巴，近义组则从命名一路走到讲清楚。

entries.definition: clear and not likely to change
to refuse openly to obey
to make something purer or better
to say what something is like
to name something exactly and clearly
entries.definitionCN: 准确而清楚地指出某事物

entries.definition: to make something easy to understand

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line drawn in the dirt and end with a word that makes a person known.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从地上画出的一条线开始，落到一个让人被认出的词。

normal.en: A field needs a fence before anyone can say whose it is.
normal.cn: 一块地要先有篱笆，才谈得上是谁的。

normal.en: To define is to draw a circle and then stand outside it to look.
normal.cn: 下定义就是画一个圈，再站到圈外看它。

normal.en: Say what a word means and you have also said what it does not.
normal.cn: 说清一个词的意思，也就说清它不是什么。

normal.en: Patience does not describe a teacher; it defines one.
normal.cn: 耐心不是描述老师，而是标示出老师。

normal.en: Finis is the end, so define puts an end to vagueness.
normal.cn: finis 是终点，所以 define 就是给含糊画上句号。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip tracing a line in dry earth.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖在干土上划出一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp held close so one page is bright and the rest is dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯凑得很近，一页亮着，其余都暗。

abstract.en: Picture a name written under a drawing, fixing what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象画下写着一个名字，把画的内容定住。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to define the word in one sentence.
examples.cn: 老师要我们用一句话说清这个词的意思。

examples.en: A low wall defines the edge of the garden.
examples.cn: 一道矮墙划出了花园的边。

examples.en: Patience defines a good teacher.
examples.cn: 耐心是好老师最鲜明的特点。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 define 记成「定分」：de 开头，fine 是「精细」，把意思定得精细，就是下定义。

root: 源自拉丁语 definire，由 de-（彻底）与 finis（界限、终点）组成，本义是绕着一块地画出界线；经古法语 definir 进入英语。界线之内是它，界线之外不是它，所以这个词既表示划定范围，也表示说清含义。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a field, to a line around a word, to the line that marks a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 从圈住一块田的线，到圈住一个词的线，再到标示一个人的那条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn around a piece of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈细线把一块地围起来。

branches.en: The first sense draws the line around a word's meaning.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把线画在一个词的含义周围。

branches.en: The same line, laid on ground, settles a border.
branches.cn: 同样的线落到地上，就定下了边界。

branches.en: Laid on a person, the line marks what is most truly his.
branches.cn: 这条线落到人身上，就标出他最真的那一面。

branches.en: Meaning and border are both made by drawing limits.
branches.cn: 含义与边界都是靠划出限度做成的。

branches.en: Both senses tell us where something begins and ends.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在告诉我们事物从哪里开始、到哪里为止。

intro.en: Define has given English a whole set of words about clear limits: definition, definite and indefinite.
intro.cn: define 给英语送来一整组关于明确界限的词：definition、definite、indefinite。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with the prefix de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.meaning: to fix the meaning or limit
items.example: The law defines the duty of the owner.
items.exampleCN: 法律界定了业主的责任。

items.example: The definition was short and exact.
items.exampleCN: 这条定义简短而准确。

items.example: We need a definite answer.
items.exampleCN: 我们需要一个明确的答复。

items.example: She will definitely come.
items.exampleCN: 她肯定会来。

items.example: The feeling was hardly definable.
items.exampleCN: 那种感觉几乎说不清。

items.example: They agreed to an indefinite wait.
items.exampleCN: 他们同意无限期等待。

items.meaning: to define again in a new way
items.example: The war redefined the border.
items.exampleCN: 这场战争重新划定了边界。

items.example: The task was well-defined.
items.exampleCN: 这项任务界定得很清楚。

definition_en: clear and fixed, not open to doubt; also easy to notice
core_image: 纸上一行字被框得方方正正，没有涂抹
scene: 她翻着日历，把下周的会面日期圈了两遍，却还留着一格空白。We still have no definite date for the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 definite 指「明确的」（第 1 个义项：清楚而不含糊）；句意是我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。

senses.title: Clear and not vague
senses.definition: stated in a way that leaves no doubt about what is meant
senses.definitionCN: 说法清楚，让人对意思没有疑问
senses.example: We still have no definite date for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。
senses.why: A word with edges can be held; a vague one slips away.
senses.whyCN: 有边的话才拿得住，含糊的话会滑走。

senses.title: Certain in one's mind
senses.definition: sure that something is true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 确信某事为真或将会发生
senses.example: She was definite about her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的回答很确定。
senses.why: Certainty is a room with the door closed.
senses.whyCN: 确定感就像一间关上了门的屋子。

senses.title: Easy to see or feel
senses.definition: large enough or strong enough to be noticed at once
senses.definitionCN: 大到或强到一眼就能察觉
senses.example: There is a definite change in the air.
senses.exampleCN: 空气里有一种明显的变化。
senses.why: What has edges also casts a shadow you cannot miss.
senses.whyCN: 有边的东西，投下的影子也让人没法忽略。

intro.en: Definite is the old past participle of define, so it carries the same picture of a line drawn around something.
intro.cn: definite 是 define 的古老过去分词，因此带着同样一幅「画线围住」的图景。

items.en: Definitus meant bounded, settled and brought to an end.
items.cn: definitus 意为有界的、定下的、已经结束的。

items.en: The word described a field with its corners marked.
items.cn: 这个词形容一块四角都标好的田。

items.en: Definit came into French as settled and certain.
items.cn: definit 进入法语时表示已定、确实。

items.en: English used it for answers, orders and grammar.
items.cn: 英语用它形容答复、命令和语法。

items.en: Grammar keeps the definite article for the one already known.
items.cn: 语法里仍用 definite article 指已经知道的那一个。

note.en: The look-alike group walks around the same fin stem, and the meaning group measures how sure a statement is.
note.cn: 形近组绕着同一个 fin 词干，近义组则衡量一句话有多确定。

entries.definition: to state the exact meaning of something
entries.definitionCN: 说明某事物的确切含义

entries.definition: final and not to be changed
having no end or limit
sure beyond doubt
easy to see or understand
named exactly rather than in general
entries.definitionCN: 具体指明的，而非笼统的

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a date circled twice and end with a change in the air nobody can miss.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从被圈了两遍的日期开始，落到空气里谁也躲不开的变化。

normal.en: A date is only a date when it is written down.
normal.cn: 日期只有写下来，才算一个日期。

normal.en: The definite article points at the cup you both already see.
normal.cn: 定冠词指的是你们都已经看见的那只杯子。

normal.en: A sure answer closes the door gently, not loudly.
normal.cn: 确定的回答是轻轻关门，而不是砰一声。

normal.en: When the air changes, you feel it before you can name it.
normal.cn: 空气一变，你先感觉到，后来才说得出。

normal.en: Definite and infinite are brothers, one with a fence and one without.
normal.cn: definite 与 infinite 是兄弟，一个带篱笆，一个没有。

abstract.en: Picture a square drawn in dust with a stick.
abstract.cn: 想象用一根树枝在灰土上画出一个方框。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a page flat so nothing moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把纸压平，什么也不许动。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow on the wall that tells you someone is near.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一道影子，告诉你有人靠近。

examples.en: We still have no definite date for the meeting.
examples.cn: 我们还没有一个明确的会议日期。

examples.en: There is a definite change in the air.
examples.cn: 空气里有一种明显的变化。

examples.en: She was definite about her answer.
examples.cn: 她对自己的回答很确定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definite 记成「定分你特」：de 开头，finite 是有限，界限分明，就是明确的。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitus，是 definire（划定界限）的过去分词，词根 finis 表示边界与终点。有边就有形，有形就不含糊，所以这个词从「划定的」引申出明确、确定与明显三层意思，语法上的定冠词也由此得名。

sensesIntro.en: From a bounded thing, to a closed mind, to a change too large to ignore.
sensesIntro.cn: 从有边有界的东西，到关上了门的心思，再到大到无法忽略的变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line drawn neatly around a word.
core.cn: 核心意象：一圈画得整整齐齐的线，围住一个词。

branches.en: The first sense is a statement with clear edges.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是边界清楚的一句话。

branches.en: The same clarity, inside a person, becomes certainty.
branches.cn: 同样的清楚放进人心里，就是确定。

branches.en: What is clearly bounded also stands out at once.
branches.cn: 界限清楚的东西，也一眼就能看出来。

branches.en: A clear answer and a sure mind are two sides of one line.
branches.cn: 清楚的答复与笃定的心思，是同一条线的两面。

branches.en: Both senses are about things that cannot be argued away.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指没法被说没的东西。

intro.en: Definite anchors a family of words about limits: define, definition, indefinite and definitive.
intro.cn: definite 撑起一族关于界限的词：define、definition、indefinite、definitive。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: Give me a definite time.
items.exampleCN: 给我一个确定的时间。

items.example: He definitely said no.
items.exampleCN: 他明确说了不行。

items.example: The definition fits the case.
items.exampleCN: 这条定义适用于这种情况。

items.example: They defined the task clearly.
items.exampleCN: 他们把任务界定得很清楚。

items.example: The definiteness of her tone surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 她语气的确定让我们吃惊。

items.example: The building stands empty for an indefinite time.
items.exampleCN: 这栋楼将无限期空置。

items.example: This is the definitive study of the river.
items.exampleCN: 这是关于这条河最权威的研究。

items.meaning: the word the, marking something known
items.meaningCN: 定冠词（指已知事物的 the）
items.example: Use the definite article before the noun.
items.exampleCN: 在这个名词前要用定冠词。

definition_en: without any doubt, or in a clear and firm way
core_image: 一句回答落地，没有留下商量的余地
scene: 朋友在门口问周末到底来不来，她一边系鞋带一边点头。I will definitely be there on Saturday.
sceneCN: 这里 definitely 指「肯定地」（第 1 个义项：毫无怀疑）；句意是星期六我一定会到。

senses.title: Without any doubt
senses.definition: used to say that something is certainly true or will happen
senses.definitionCN: 用来说明某事确实为真或一定发生
senses.example: I will definitely be there on Saturday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期六我一定会到。
senses.why: A promise with no space left in it is easier to keep.
senses.whyCN: 没留空隙的承诺，反而更容易守住。

senses.title: In a clear and firm way
senses.definition: in a manner that leaves no room for another reading
senses.definitionCN: 所说的话不容许别的理解
senses.example: She spoke definitely about the closing date.
senses.exampleCN: 她把截止日期说得很明确。
senses.why: Firm speech is a line that does not bend when pressed.
senses.whyCN: 坚定的说法，是一条压也不弯的线。

senses.title: As a warm yes in talk
senses.definition: used in speech to agree strongly with a suggestion
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用于强烈赞同某个提议
senses.example: Definitely, let us take the early train.
senses.exampleCN: 当然，我们就坐早班车。
senses.why: Agreement, said with force, becomes a small gift.
senses.whyCN: 用力说出的赞同，就是一份小小的礼物。

intro.en: Definitely is definite plus -ly; its parents are Latin finis, a boundary, and the prefix de-.
intro.cn: definitely 是 definite 加 -ly，父母是拉丁语的 finis（边界）与前缀 de-。

items.en: Definitus meant bounded and settled.
items.cn: definitus 意为有界的、已定的。

items.en: Definit reached French with the sense of certain.
items.cn: definit 带着「确实」的意思进入法语。

items.en: Definite settled into English as an adjective.
items.cn: definite 作为形容词在英语里安定下来。

items.en: The adverb definitely appeared in letters and records.
items.cn: 副词 definitely 出现在书信与文书里。

items.en: In speech it has become a friendly, emphatic yes.
items.cn: 在口语里它已经变成一个热情而强调的「是」。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by small endings, and the meaning group is made of three ways to say for sure.
note.cn: 形近组只差很小的词尾，近义组则由三种「说准了」的方式组成。

entries.definition: clear and not open to doubt

openly refusing to obey

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a nod at the door and end with an agreement that sounds like a gift.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从门口的一个点头开始，落到听起来像礼物的赞同。

normal.en: A yes said slowly is worth more than a maybe said often.
normal.cn: 慢慢说出的「是」，比常常说的「也许」更值钱。

normal.en: A date given definitely can be written in ink.
normal.cn: 说得肯定的日期，才可以拿钢笔写。

normal.en: When the answer is clear, the voice drops instead of rising.
normal.cn: 答案清楚时，声音是往下落，不是往上扬。

normal.en: Definitely carries a line at its middle; that line is the fence.
normal.cn: definitely 中间带着一条线，那条线就是篱笆。

normal.en: Add -ly to definite and certainty becomes a way of speaking.
normal.cn: definite 加 -ly，确定就成了一种说话方式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand laid flat on a table to end a discussion.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手平放在桌上，把讨论按住。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence written in ink with no eraser nearby.
abstract.cn: 想象一句用墨水写下的话，旁边没有橡皮。

abstract.en: Picture a nod given before the question is finished.
abstract.cn: 想象问题还没说完，头已经点下去了。

examples.cn: 星期六我一定会到。

examples.en: She spoke definitely about the closing date.

examples.en: Definitely, let us take the early train.

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definitely 记成「定分你特利」：定得分明，说话才干脆，就是肯定地。

root: 由 definite 加副词词尾 -ly 构成，而 definite 来自拉丁语 definitus（有界的、已定的），词根 finis 是边界。界线一画定，说话就不留余地，因此这个词既表示毫无疑问，也表示语气明确，口语里还成了热情的「当然」。

sensesIntro.en: From a promise with no gap, to a firm sentence, to a warm yes at the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 从没有缝隙的承诺，到一句坚定的说明，再到门口那声热情的「当然」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an answer that lands flat and stays.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句回答落地，就停在那里不动。

branches.en: The first sense is certainty about what will happen.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是对将要发生之事的确定。

branches.en: The same certainty, in the mouth, becomes firm speech.
branches.cn: 同样的确定进了嘴里，就是坚定的说法。

branches.en: Said to a friend, the firm word turns into warmth.
branches.cn: 对朋友说出时，坚定的词就变成了暖意。

branches.en: Both senses refuse to leave a door open for doubt.
branches.cn: 两个义项都不肯给怀疑留一扇门。

branches.en: A firm answer and a warm yes are the same word at different heat.
branches.cn: 坚定的答复与热情的赞同，是同一个词的不同温度。

intro.en: Definitely is built from definite and -ly, and the family around it is all about limits.
intro.cn: definitely 由 definite 与 -ly 构成，周围那一族词全都与界限有关。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with the prefix de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: We made a definite plan.
items.exampleCN: 我们定了一个明确的计划。

items.example: The definition is easy to remember.
items.exampleCN: 这条定义容易记。

items.example: He defined the rule for us.
items.exampleCN: 他为我们讲清了规则。

items.example: There was definiteness in her voice.
items.exampleCN: 她的声音里有确定。

items.example: They chose an indefinite pause.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择了无限期的暂停。

items.example: The report is definitive on this point.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告在这一点上已成定论。

items.example: That is definitely not the answer.
items.exampleCN: 那肯定不是答案。

definition_en: a statement of what a word or idea means; also the sharpness of an image
core_image: 词典上一行小字，把一个词钉住
scene: 她把词典摊在膝上，指尖顺着两行小字往下滑。The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
sceneCN: 这里 definition 指「释义」（第 1 个义项：说明词义的语句）；句意是词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

senses.title: A statement of meaning
senses.definition: a sentence that says exactly what a word or idea means
senses.definitionCN: 准确说明一个词或概念含义的句子
senses.example: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。
senses.why: A word without a definition is a door without a key.
senses.whyCN: 没有定义的词，就像没有钥匙的门。

senses.title: The act of marking limits
senses.definition: the act of fixing the border or scope of something
senses.definitionCN: 确定某事物的边界或范围的行为
senses.example: The definition of the study area took a month.
senses.exampleCN: 划定研究区域用了一个月。
senses.why: Before a thing can be studied, its edge must be agreed on.
senses.whyCN: 要研究一样东西，先得商量好它的边在哪儿。

senses.title: Sharpness of an image
senses.definition: the clearness of an image or sound on a screen
senses.definitionCN: 屏幕上的画面或声音清楚的程度
senses.example: The old film was restored in high definition.
senses.exampleCN: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。
senses.why: A sharp edge is what the eye and the mind both call clear.
senses.whyCN: 边缘锐利，眼睛和脑子都会说它清楚。

intro.en: Definition comes from Latin definitio, a bounding, from finis, a limit, and de-, completely.
intro.cn: definition 来自拉丁语 definitio（划定边界），出自 finis（界限）与 de-（彻底）。

items.en: Finis marked the end of a field or the close of a speech.
items.cn: finis 指一块田的尽头，也指一段话的收尾。

items.en: Definitio was the act of drawing a thing's border.
items.cn: definitio 是给事物画出边界的行为。

items.en: Definicion carried the word into law and learning.
items.cn: definicion 把这个词带进法律与学问。

items.en: English used it for the meaning given in a dictionary.
items.cn: 英语用它指词典里给出的意思。

items.en: Film and screens added the sense of a sharp picture.
items.cn: 电影与屏幕又给它添了画面清晰这一层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fin stem, and the meaning group names what a definition gives to a reader.
note.cn: 形近组共用 fin 词干，近义组则说出定义交给读者的东西。

entries.definition: final and accepted as the best
clear and certain
to say what something means
words that make something understood
what a word or sign stands for
entries.definitionCN: 词或符号所代表的内容

entries.definition: a picture made with words

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a finger running down a dictionary and end with a picture sharp enough to touch.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从沿着词典往下滑的指尖开始，落到清晰得几乎能摸到的画面。

normal.en: A definition is a small fence built around a large word.
normal.cn: 定义就是给一个大词围起来的一道小篱笆。

normal.en: Two definitions for one word mean two doors into the same house.
normal.cn: 一个词有两条释义，就是同一间屋子的两扇门。

normal.en: You cannot count what you have not first bounded.
normal.cn: 没有先划出范围，就没法数清里面有多少。

normal.en: A high definition picture is just a picture with cleaner edges.
normal.cn: 高清画面，不过是边缘更干净的画面。

normal.en: Definition is the noun that define leaves behind.
normal.cn: definition 就是 define 留下的那个名词。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip stopping under one line of small print.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖停在一行小字下面。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on grass to mark where the tent goes.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上拉一根绳，标出帐篷该搭在哪。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf on a screen with every vein in view.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一片叶子，每根叶脉都看得见。

examples.en: The dictionary gives two definitions of the word.
examples.cn: 词典给出了这个词的两条释义。

examples.en: By definition, a square has four equal sides.
examples.cn: 按照定义，正方形有四条相等的边。

examples.en: The old film was restored in high definition.
examples.cn: 这部老片子被修复成了高清。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 definition 记成「定分神」：定得分明，一句话就把词钉住，神都跑了，定义却留下。

root: 源自拉丁语 definitio，出自 definire（划定界限），词根 finis 表示边界与终点。先有「画线」这个动作，才有「划出的范围」，再有「说明词义的语句」；近代摄影与屏幕又借它表示图像的清晰度。

sensesIntro.en: From a line around a word, to the act of drawing it, to the edge of a picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 从围住一个词的那条线，到画线的动作，再到画面的边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small fence built around one word.
core.cn: 核心意象：围着一个词搭起的一小圈篱笆。

branches.en: The first sense is the sentence that fences a word.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是把词围起来的那句话。

branches.en: The second sense is the act of building that fence.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是搭起这道篱笆的动作。

branches.en: On a screen, the fence becomes a clean edge.
branches.cn: 在屏幕上，这道篱笆变成了干净的边。

branches.en: A statement and the act behind it are one thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 一句话和它背后的动作，是同一件事的两种看法。

branches.en: Both senses are about making a shape stand out from its background.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是让形状从背景里站出来。

intro.en: Definition belongs to the finis family, with define, definite, definitive and indefinite beside it.
intro.cn: definition 属于 finis 这一族，旁边还有 define、definite、definitive、indefinite。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is finis, a boundary, with de- meaning completely.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 finis（边界），前缀 de- 表示彻底。

items.example: The definition runs to three lines.
items.exampleCN: 这条释义写了三行。

items.example: The book defines every term it uses.
items.exampleCN: 这本书给每个用到的术语都下了定义。

items.example: We need a definite answer today.
items.exampleCN: 我们今天需要一个明确答复。

items.example: She definitely understood the rule.
items.exampleCN: 她肯定明白了规则。

items.example: It is now the definitive account.
items.exampleCN: 它如今是权威的说法。

items.meaning: about the meaning of a term
items.example: The dispute was definitional.
items.exampleCN: 这场争论是定义上的分歧。

items.example: The law needs a redefinition of duty.
items.exampleCN: 这条法律需要重新界定责任。

items.example: They watched the match in high definition.
items.exampleCN: 他们看的是高清比赛。

definition_en: a level or amount of something; a unit of measurement; a title given by a university
core_image: 温度计上的刻度，一格一格往上
scene: 炉子上的水开始翻滚，壶嘴喷出白气，窗户蒙上一层雾。Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
sceneCN: 这里 degree 指「度」（第 1 个义项：测量温度的单位）；句意是水在一百度时沸腾。

senses.title: A level or amount
senses.definition: the level or amount of a quality or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 某种性质或感受所处的水平与分量
senses.example: I agree with you to some degree.
senses.exampleCN: 我在某种程度上同意你。
senses.why: Almost nothing is simply yes or no; there are steps between.
senses.whyCN: 很少有事情只是是与非，中间还有一级一级的台阶。

senses.title: A unit on a scale
senses.definition: a unit used to measure temperature, angle or height
senses.definitionCN: 测量温度、角度或高度的单位
senses.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
senses.exampleCN: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。
senses.why: To compare heat or turn, people first had to cut the scale into steps.
senses.whyCN: 要比较冷热或转角，先得把刻度切成格。

senses.title: A title from a university
senses.definition: a rank given by a university to someone who has finished a course
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予完成学业者的等级称号
senses.example: She earned a degree in history last year.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年拿到了历史学学位。
senses.why: Learning also climbs, and the top of the climb gets a name.
senses.whyCN: 学问也是一步步往上走，走到顶上就该有个名号。

intro.en: Degree goes back to Latin gradus, a step, through Old French degre, a rank on a ladder.
intro.cn: degree 上溯到拉丁语 gradus（台阶），经古法语 degre（梯子上的等级）进入英语。

items.en: Gradus meant a step, a pace or a rung of a ladder.
items.cn: gradus 指一步、一步的距离，或梯子的一级。

items.en: Degre named a rank and a step upward.
items.cn: degre 指等级，也指向上的一级。

items.en: English used it for steps of heat and of honour.
items.cn: 英语用它讲冷热的级差，也讲身份的等级。

items.en: Universities began to award degrees as ranks of learning.
items.cn: 大学开始用学位标示学问的等级。

items.en: The word now measures temperature, angles, feelings and study.
items.cn: 如今它量温度、量角度，也量情感与学问。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the gre sound, and the meaning group is made of words for how much of something there is.
note.cn: 形近组共用 gre 这个音，近义组则是几个表示「有多少」的词。

entries.definition: a level of quality or a class in school
entries.definitionCN: 质量等级或学校里的年级

entries.definition: an official order made by a ruler
entries.definitionCN: 统治者发布的正式命令

entries.definition: to lower someone's rank or worth
entries.definitionCN: 降低某人的等级或价值

entries.definition: a height or standard reached
how far something reaches or happens
entries.definitionCN: 某事物延伸或发生的范围

entries.definition: how much there is of something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a thermometer climbing and end with a name given at the top of the climb.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从往上爬的温度计开始，落到爬到顶上领到的那个名号。

normal.en: A ladder is only useful because it has steps.
normal.cn: 梯子之所以有用，就因为有一级一级。

normal.en: Hot and cold are not two things but two ends of one line.
normal.cn: 冷和热不是两样东西，而是一条线的两头。

normal.en: A degree in hand is a step turned into a name.
normal.cn: 手里的学位，就是把一级台阶换成了名号。

normal.en: By degrees is the only way a tree grows.
normal.cn: 树只能一点点长，这就是逐渐。

normal.en: Grade and degree both come from the same step.
normal.cn: grade 与 degree 都是从同一级台阶来的。

abstract.en: Picture a red line rising in a thin glass tube.
abstract.cn: 想象细玻璃管里一条红线往上走。

abstract.en: Picture a rope ladder with a name tied to the top rung.
abstract.cn: 想象一架绳梯，最高一级上系着一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture a winter room warmed one step at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象冬天的屋子，一格一格暖起来。

examples.en: Water boils at one hundred degrees Celsius.
examples.cn: 水在一百摄氏度沸腾。

examples.en: I agree with you to some degree.
examples.cn: 我在某种程度上同意你。

examples.en: She earned a degree in history last year.
examples.cn: 她去年拿到了历史学学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 degree 记成「地格瑞」：地上一格一格往上走，每一格就是一个程度。

root: 源自拉丁语 gradus（一步、一级台阶），经古法语 degre 进入英语。台阶既能量冷热，也能量身份与学问：于是它同时表示程度、度数与学位；by degrees 保留了「一级一级走」的老画面。

sensesIntro.en: From a rung on a ladder, to a mark on a scale, to a title at the top of study.
sensesIntro.cn: 从梯子上的一级，到刻度上的一格，再到学问顶端的名号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of marks climbing up a glass tube.
core.cn: 核心意象：玻璃管上一格一格往上爬的刻度。

branches.en: The first sense is how far along the scale a quality sits.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是某种性质在刻度上走到哪一格。

branches.en: The second sense is the mark itself, used for heat and angle.
branches.cn: 第二个义项就是那一格刻度，量冷热也量角度。

branches.en: Climbed far enough in study, a person receives a rank.
branches.cn: 在学问上爬得够高，人就会得到一个等级。

branches.en: A feeling and a temperature are both read off the same ladder.
branches.cn: 感受与温度，都是沿着同一架梯子读出来的。

branches.en: Both senses turn a smooth climb into countable steps.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把连续的攀升切成可数的格。

intro.en: Degree shares its Latin step with gradual, graduate and degrade, a whole family of climbing words.
intro.cn: degree 与 gradual、graduate、degrade 共用拉丁语「台阶」这个词根，是一整族往上走的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is gradus, a step, from gradi, to walk.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 gradus（台阶），出自 gradi（行走）。

items.example: The temperature rose by ten degrees.
items.exampleCN: 温度上升了十度。

items.example: There was a gradual change in colour.
items.exampleCN: 颜色有逐渐的变化。

items.example: The room gradually grew warm.
items.exampleCN: 屋里渐渐暖和起来。

items.meaning: to finish a course of study
items.example: He will graduate next June.
items.exampleCN: 他明年六月毕业。

items.meaning: a small step or shade of difference
items.example: The sky showed fine gradations of grey.
items.exampleCN: 天空呈现出细腻的灰度层次。

items.example: The chemical degrades in sunlight.
items.exampleCN: 这种化学品在阳光下会分解。

items.meaning: to raise to a higher level
items.example: They upgraded the old system.
items.exampleCN: 他们升级了旧系统。

items.example: By degrees the noise died away.
items.exampleCN: 声音渐渐地消失了。
